item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Short interest in the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, is up to ~82 million shares, its highest sinc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Short interest in the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, is up to ~82 million shares, its highest since March 2023.
Over the last several weeks, this figure has surged +18 million shares, or +28%.
Year-to-date, short interest in $QQQ has nearly doubled.
Meanwhile, short interest in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, has declined -30 million shares since March, to ~92 million shares, near its lowest in at least 5 years.
By comparison, during the 2022 bear market, short interest peaked at ~90 million shares for $QQQ and ~180 million shares for $SPY.
Short interest in tech is very high right now.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On days like today, it's important to zoom out. No, the AI Revolution is not "over," and the market...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On days like today, it's important to zoom out.
No, the AI Revolution is not "over," and the market is not "going to zero."
In fact, the Nasdaq 100 is up +11% YTD and nearly +70% since its April 2025 low.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is currently set to post a blended earnings +30.2% growth rate for Q3 2026.
This puts us on track for the third-straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
And, even after the biggest hack in crypto history, Bitcoin is down less than -5% this week.
Disruptive technologies like AI will inevitably bring heightened volatility, polarized positioning, and extreme swings in market sentiment.
However, do not let short-term volatility overshadow the broader picture.
We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in history.
Technical corrections are healthy, necessary, and an inevitable part of every bull market.
Do not lose sight of the bigger picture.

item.title: @wallstengine: $TSLA EXPECTED TO OPEN OPTIMUS ROBOT RESERVATIONS IN EARLY DECEMBER: REPORT Tesla is reportedly pre...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$TSLA EXPECTED TO OPEN OPTIMUS ROBOT RESERVATIONS IN EARLY DECEMBER: REPORT
Tesla is reportedly preparing to open consumer reservations for its Optimus humanoid robot in early December, potentially around the December 1-2 Humanoids Summit, according to The San Francisco Standard.
Tesla is also expected to demonstrate Optimus V3 at the event, with most initial units intended for businesses and a smaller number reserved for consumers.
The robot is expected to cost more than $20,000, although reservation deposits and final pricing remain unclear.
Tesla has already begun early production at its Fremont factory, but Musk recently said deliveries to outside customers aren't expected until late 2027, as the company continues working through AI, hardware and reliability challenges.
Tesla has not officially confirmed the reservation plans.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC IN TALKS TO LEASE MAJOR AI DATA CENTER CAMPUS IN 🇨🇦 CANADA: GLOBE & MAIL Anthropic is r...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC IN TALKS TO LEASE MAJOR AI DATA CENTER CAMPUS IN 🇨🇦 CANADA: GLOBE & MAIL
Anthropic is reportedly negotiating with Beacon Data Centers to lease a large AI data center campus near Edmonton, Alberta.
The proposed site would feature four data halls powered by a 920 MW natural gas plant, which received regulatory approval on October 23.
Construction of the power plant is expected to begin in Q4 2026, with operations targeted for Q4 2027.
The potential deal comes just two weeks after Anthropic signed a 20-year lease for a separate 420 MW data center project in Nova Scotia.
The Alberta project would have roughly twice the power capacity of the Nova Scotia campus, adding to Anthropic's growing infrastructure commitments ahead of its planned IPO.
Talks remain ongoing, and no agreement has been announced.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy. As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is no...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy.
As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is now down nearly -5% on the day.
Meanwhile, the market-implied odds of a Democrat "sweep" in the Midterms next week has surged from 65% to 72% today, a record high.
That's +7 percentage points in 2 days amid this market downturn.
We have yet to receive a comment from the Trump Administration regarding the current situation in the market.
However, what is clear is that the timing of today's market crash will be consequential.
And, even as technology stocks drop sharply, US Treasury Yields are barely seeing any relief.
This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation.
Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Okay, this is pretty cool.
You can now have all your AI agents working together in a virtual office.
Skydive gives each agent its own cloud computer and a place inside a 3D workspace.
You can actually see your agents, click on them to check what they're working on, read their conversations, and assign new tasks.
They can also work across tools like Slack, Gmail, Notion, and GitHub, with memory that carries over between sessions.
Basically, instead of juggling a bunch of AI chat windows, you can manage your entire AI team from one virtual office.

item.title: @wallstengine: KALSHI RAISES $1B AT A $40 BILLION VALUATION Kalshi has closed a Series G co-led by Sequoia Capital...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
KALSHI RAISES $1B AT A $40 BILLION VALUATION
Kalshi has closed a Series G co-led by Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management.
Its valuation has climbed from $1B in June 2025 to $40B in just sixteen months.
Kalshi launched in 2021 after spending nearly four years securing federal regulation. It gained traction during the 2024 election, then reached a much wider audience after introducing sports contracts in early 2025.
Growth is now increasingly driven by markets beyond sports, including crypto, commodities, and new derivatives products:
"Kalshi continues to experience significant growth, with Q4 revenue currently on track to surpass Robinhood's revenue."
The new capital will support new products for retail and institutional customers, and international expansion.
Other investors include Morgan Stanley Investment Management, Baillie Gifford, Coatue and Andreessen Horowitz.
An IPO has also been discussed, though Tarek Mansour has not confirmed plans or provided a timeline.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Anthropic is now expected to receive a "high junk" rating from major credit rating agenci...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Anthropic is now expected to receive a "high junk" rating from major credit rating agencies after its IPO, which could come as soon as November, per FT.
Details include:
1. Blackstone has told investors that Anthropic likely will not receive an investment-grade rating immediately after its IPO
2. Blackstone is working with banks that stumped up financing on selling the debt on to other investors
3. An investment-grade rating is "central" to Anthropic's ability to continue its AI buildout
4. The company says it expects to spend over $800 billion on computing infrastructure between now and 2045
Debt markets are increasingly in the spotlight as AI funding becomes less abundant.

item.title: @wallstengine: Ford $F CEO Jim Farley is targeting 5 million annual vehicle sales by 2032, roughly 20% above curre...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Ford $F CEO Jim Farley is targeting 5 million annual vehicle sales by 2032, roughly 20% above current levels.
Ford hasn't reached that volume since 2019, and its global vehicle deliveries are down 9% so far this year.
The company plans to introduce five new models priced below $40,000 by the end of the decade, including its $30,000 Fathom electric pickup, which is expected to begin production in Q4 2027.
Ford is targeting more than 100,000 Fathom sales in its first year, while also expanding its lineup in Europe through partnerships with Renault and Geely.
Source: WSJ
item.content:encoded:
Ford $F CEO Jim Farley is targeting 5 million annual vehicle sales by 2032, roughly 20% above current levels.

Ford hasn't reached that volume since 2019, and its global vehicle deliveries are down 9% so far this year.

The company plans to introduce five new models priced below $40,000 by the end of the decade, including its $30,000 Fathom electric pickup, which is expected to begin production in Q4 2027.

Ford is targeting more than 100,000 Fathom sales in its first year, while also expanding its lineup in Europe through partnerships with Renault and Geely.

Source: WSJ

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT Blackstone has told investo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT
Blackstone has told investors Anthropic is likely to receive a credit rating in the double-B range after going public, below investment grade, reversing its earlier expectations for an investment-grade rating by year-end.
The lower rating could make it more expensive for Anthropic to finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, while limiting access to pension funds and insurers that face restrictions on investing in junk-rated debt.
The warning comes as Blackstone participates in Anthropic's $63B financing deal, known as Project North Star, to support the leasing of 1.5 GW of Google's AI chips.
Under the deal:
• More than $42B in senior loans are guaranteed by Broadcom $AVGO.
• Another $18B in junior debt is backed by Anthropic's lease payments.
• Blackstone's funds invested $9B in junior debt, earning yields above 10%.
Anthropic's IPO prospectus outlined plans to spend more than $800B on computing infrastructure through 2045.
Without an investment-grade rating, Anthropic may need to continue relying on financially stronger partners to support its borrowing.
The major credit agencies, Moody's, S&P and Fitch, have not yet formally issued ratings for Anthropic, per FT.

item.title: @wallstengine: Global Payments $GPN is being targeted in a potential $40B+ buyout by private equity firm Clayton,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Global Payments $GPN is being targeted in a potential $40B+ buyout by private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, which has teamed up with GTCR, the company's largest shareholder, FT reports.
The payments processor has a market value of roughly $23B and more than $17B in net debt. A deal including a takeover premium would rank among the largest leveraged buyouts in history.
Interestingly, GTCR became Global Payments' largest outside shareholder through its 2025 Worldpay acquisition, a deal that drew investor criticism over increased debt and dilution.
Global Payments shares subsequently fell to near-decade lows, attracting activist investor Elliott Management.
Talks are ongoing, and no agreement has been reached.

item.title: @wallstengine: Starbucks $SBUX CEO Brian Niccol says the company could eventually expand beyond coffee and become...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Starbucks $SBUX CEO Brian Niccol says the company could eventually expand beyond coffee and become a multi-brand business, similar to Yum Brands, which owns Taco Bell and KFC.
“Our scale provides an opportunity to go beyond just being a one-brand company.”
“You put other businesses into a portfolio that can leverage the strength of Starbucks — that could be an interesting proposition, down the road.”
Niccol added that he would “never say never” to acquisitions, although Starbucks remains focused on its own turnaround and doesn't need deals to meet its growth targets.
The comments come weeks after Starbucks dismissed rumors of a potential Chipotle takeover.

item.title: @wallstengine: $INTC -30%; on track for its worst day since 1974 Intel's Q3 earnings beat was overshadowed by a br...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$INTC -30%; on track for its worst day since 1974
Intel's Q3 earnings beat was overshadowed by a broad Q4 outlook miss, with revenue, EPS and gross margin forecasts all falling well below Wall Street expectations.
The biggest problem is the PC business, which has slowed much faster than management anticipated over the past two months.
Intel now expects PC-related revenue to fall more than 20% sequentially in Q4.
Rising memory prices are making computers more expensive, weakening demand and forcing PC manufacturers to cut chip orders as they work through excess inventory.
Management expects the inventory correction to continue into H1 2027, potentially extending into Q2, while projecting another 10% decline in industry PC shipments next year.
CFO Dave Zinsner:
“We are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory.”
Meanwhile, data-center revenue surged 78%, but Intel is struggling to meet demand due to manufacturing and advanced packaging shortages. Meaningful capacity relief isn't expected until the second half of 2027.
Adding to the pressure, an accident at Intel's Fab 28 facility in Israel is expected to reduce revenue by approximately $300M in both Q4 and Q1, while cutting Q4 gross margin by roughly 200 basis points.
Intel also plans to increase capital spending significantly from this year's $20B as it expands manufacturing capacity, and does not expect positive free cash flow in 2027.
The challenge is that Intel's PC business is weakening just as demand for its server chips is accelerating, but supply constraints are preventing the company from fully capitalizing on that growth.
item.content:encoded:
$INTC -30%; on track for its worst day since 1974

Intel's Q3 earnings beat was overshadowed by a broad Q4 outlook miss, with revenue, EPS and gross margin forecasts all falling well below Wall Street expectations.

The biggest problem is the PC business, which has slowed much faster than management anticipated over the past two months.

Intel now expects PC-related revenue to fall more than 20% sequentially in Q4.

Rising memory prices are making computers more expensive, weakening demand and forcing PC manufacturers to cut chip orders as they work through excess inventory.

Management expects the inventory correction to continue into H1 2027, potentially extending into Q2, while projecting another 10% decline in industry PC shipments next year.

CFO Dave Zinsner:

“We are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory.”

Meanwhile, data-center revenue surged 78%, but Intel is struggling to meet demand due to manufacturing and advanced packaging shortages. Meaningful capacity relief isn't expected until the second half of 2027.

Adding to the pressure, an accident at Intel's Fab 28 facility in Israel is expected to reduce revenue by approximately $300M in both Q4 and Q1, while cutting Q4 gross margin by roughly 200 basis points.

Intel also plans to increase capital spending significantly from this year's $20B as it expands manufacturing capacity, and does not expect positive free cash flow in 2027.

The challenge is that Intel's PC business is weakening just as demand for its server chips is accelerating, but supply constraints are preventing the company from fully capitalizing on that growth.

The Biological Computing Co. spent 4 years studying neurons grown on electrodes, then applied those discoveries to its first video model, mischief 1.
Upload an image, describe what should happen, and generate a five-second, 720p video. TBC says it’s at least 5x faster than its base model, with a starting cost of 2.5 cents per clip.
It’s built for experimentation rather than competing with the highest-end video models: test ad hooks, sketch storyboards or try different scenes before committing to a production-quality render.
The model itself runs on regular chips.
Available on fal and OpenRouter, with AWS Marketplace planned.
Launch video by Wonder Studios. https://x.com/AlexKsendzovsky/status/2116153410101944352/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: Counterpoint says global smartphone processor shipments fell 21% YoY in Q3 as rising memory costs p...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Counterpoint says global smartphone processor shipments fell 21% YoY in Q3 as rising memory costs pushed manufacturers to cut cheaper models.
• MediaTek's market share fell from 34% to 28% • Qualcomm's $QCOM declined from 25% to 22% • Apple's increased from 17% to 21%
Qualcomm also faced pressure from Samsung using its own Exynos chips in some Galaxy S26 models, alongside weaker sales from Chinese smartphone makers.
Counterpoint now expects smartphone chip shipments to decline 20% in 2026 and another 3%-4% in 2027.

item.title: @wallstengine: BofA removes Apple $AAPL from its U.S. 1 List, cuts iPhone sales estimates & warns Wall St. is sign...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BofA removes Apple $AAPL from its U.S. 1 List, cuts iPhone sales estimates & warns Wall St. is significantly underestimating the impact of rising memory prices on margins.
“We lower our F27 iPhone est. by 9mn units to 247mn (vs. St at 260mn).”
BofA estimates memory costs could reduce iPhone gross margins by 900 basis points before offsets, or roughly 500 basis points after pricing, product mix and cost adjustments.
That translates to an estimated 250-basis-point hit to companywide gross margins.
The bank now projects Apple's total gross margin at 43.6%-44.6% by the March quarter, well below Wall Street's 47.7% estimate.

item.title: @wallstengine: Roblox $RBLX -17% Falling on weaker Q4 guidance and higher AI spending, despite better-than-expecte...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Roblox $RBLX -17%
Falling on weaker Q4 guidance and higher AI spending, despite better-than-expected Q3 results.
Roblox expects bookings to decline 10%-15% YoY in Q4, following a 12% decline in Q3. Its adjusted EBITDA outlook is roughly 13% below consensus at the midpoint, according to BMO.
Management is not assuming an immediate improvement in monetization and has included a modest headwind from GTA VI, while acknowledging limited evidence to estimate its impact.
The company is also increasing spending on AI infrastructure and marketing to adult users. Another $140M in capital spending shifted from Q3 into Q4, helping Q3 cash flow but weighing on the coming quarter.
Meanwhile, engagement improved: daily users rose 12% from Q2 to 138M, and seasonally adjusted retention reached its highest level since 2021.
Roblox says more than 80% of its top 100 games by hours played used AI during development. Its Build AI game-creation tool is scheduled for a broader U.S. release in December, but the timing of a meaningful financial payoff remains uncertain.
item.content:encoded:
Roblox $RBLX -17%

Falling on weaker Q4 guidance and higher AI spending, despite better-than-expected Q3 results.

Roblox expects bookings to decline 10%-15% YoY in Q4, following a 12% decline in Q3. Its adjusted EBITDA outlook is roughly 13% below consensus at the midpoint, according to BMO.

Management is not assuming an immediate improvement in monetization and has included a modest headwind from GTA VI, while acknowledging limited evidence to estimate its impact.

The company is also increasing spending on AI infrastructure and marketing to adult users. Another $140M in capital spending shifted from Q3 into Q4, helping Q3 cash flow but weighing on the coming quarter.

Meanwhile, engagement improved: daily users rose 12% from Q2 to 138M, and seasonally adjusted retention reached its highest level since 2021.

Roblox says more than 80% of its top 100 games by hours played used AI during development. Its Build AI game-creation tool is scheduled for a broader U.S. release in December, but the timing of a meaningful financial payoff remains uncertain.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Reddit's earnings call has exposed the new reality for thousands of companies. "AI mode does not dr...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Reddit's earnings call has exposed the new reality for thousands of companies.
"AI mode does not drive traffic. Not for us and not to anybody as far as I know. It used to be a traffic driver. Now it's not." - Reddit CEO.
The reality is that AI is fundamentally changing the way that humans access the internet.
Just 24 hours prior to this statement, Google's stock erased -$480 billion on the same issue: AI is disrupting the traditional search model.
For decades, the internet operated on a simple model. Search engines directed users to websites, and those websites monetized the traffic.
AI is destroying this business model, and it's happening at an accelerating pace.
The traditional model of internet traffic is rapidly becoming outdated.
The internet has entered a new era.

item.title: @wallstengine: $INTC is reportedly developing a new ultra-low-power processor called Moon Lake, potentially replac...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$INTC is reportedly developing a new ultra-low-power processor called Moon Lake, potentially replacing its N-series chips used in budget laptops & mini PCs.
The chip would feature:
• 4 Darkmont low-power efficiency cores • No performance cores • Intel's 18A mfg. process • 6W base power, configurable up to 15W • Same BGA1516 package as Wildcat Lake
For comparison, Intel's current Wildcat Lake processors feature up to two performance cores and four low-power efficiency cores, with a 15W base power rating.
Moon Lake appears designed to prioritize low power consumption over peak performance.
Intel has not officially confirmed the chip, its specifications or a launch date.
Source: Jaykihn (leaker)

item.title: @wallstengine: Rivian $RIVN +9% Following better-than-expected Q3 earnings, raised full-year guidance. The biggest...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Rivian $RIVN +9%
Following better-than-expected Q3 earnings, raised full-year guidance.
The biggest development is Rivian's R2, which became its best-selling vehicle in its first full quarter, outselling both R1 and its commercial vans.
Total deliveries reached a record 19,248, up 46% YoY. Management says R2 reservation conversions are exceeding expectations, while demo drives jumped to 103K from 57K in Q2.
Rivian has also started a second R2 production shift, with manufacturing costs per vehicle falling by over $12,000 sequentially, although its automotive business remains unprofitable.
Meanwhile:
• Adj EBITDA loss: $435M vs. $591M expected • FY26 deliveries raised to 67K-70K from 65K-70K
• FY26 capex lowered to $1.4B-$1.5B from $1.7B-$1.8B, mainly due to spending timing
Rivian also plans a limited rollout of supervised point-to-point driving later this year, followed by broader availability in 2027.
Its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day is another catalyst, alongside a potential $250M Uber investment milestone expected by year-end.
item.content:encoded:
Rivian $RIVN +9%

Following better-than-expected Q3 earnings, raised full-year guidance.

The biggest development is Rivian's R2, which became its best-selling vehicle in its first full quarter, outselling both R1 and its commercial vans.

Total deliveries reached a record 19,248, up 46% YoY. Management says R2 reservation conversions are exceeding expectations, while demo drives jumped to 103K from 57K in Q2.

Rivian has also started a second R2 production shift, with manufacturing costs per vehicle falling by over $12,000 sequentially, although its automotive business remains unprofitable.

Meanwhile:

• Adj EBITDA loss: $435M vs. $591M expected

Rivian also plans a limited rollout of supervised point-to-point driving later this year, followed by broader availability in 2027.

Its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day is another catalyst, alongside a potential $250M Uber investment milestone expected by year-end.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: New details on how the $6.3 billion Binance hack likely occurred: According to initial reports, hac...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
New details on how the $6.3 billion Binance hack likely occurred:
According to initial reports, hackers compromised a Binance engineer's laptop, gaining access to internal systems used to authorize withdrawals.
The attackers then:
1. Hijacked a Binance hot wallet using Ethereum's EIP-7702 mechanism
2. Redirected wallet transactions to a malicious smart contract
3. Transferred billions in crypto attacker-controlled wallets
4. Spread the stolen funds across multiple wallets and converted some assets into ETH to avoid freezes
The attack unfolded across multiple blockchains, with most funds drained in ~20 minutes.
~$3 billion of these funds have now been frozen, and Binance says it will cover all unrecovered hacking losses.
The full investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: @wallstengine: BINANCE FACES WHAT COULD BE THE BIGGEST CRYPTO HACK IN HISTORY Blockchain researchers spotted billi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BINANCE FACES WHAT COULD BE THE BIGGEST CRYPTO HACK IN HISTORY
Blockchain researchers spotted billions of dollars in suspicious transfers from Binance's hot wallets to newly created addresses, with some funds quickly moved to other wallets.
One of the initial Ethereum transfers involved roughly $1.6B in USDT and 167,000 ETH.
Estimates of total suspicious outflows have now reached approximately $5.9B across multiple blockchain networks, although the amount actually stolen remains unconfirmed.
In response, Tether and Circle have frozen more than $2.38B in stablecoins linked to the incident, preventing those funds from being transferred further.
Binance founder CZ says it “does look like a hack” and expects customer funds to be fully covered.
Binance says user funds remain safe and is investigating the security issue. Some customers have also experienced withdrawal disruptions.
For context, the previous largest crypto hack was the $1.5B Bybit theft in February 2025.
If the full reported amount is confirmed stolen, this would surpass that record by nearly four times.
item.content:encoded:
BINANCE FACES WHAT COULD BE THE BIGGEST CRYPTO HACK IN HISTORY

Blockchain researchers spotted billions of dollars in suspicious transfers from Binance's hot wallets to newly created addresses, with some funds quickly moved to other wallets.

One of the initial Ethereum transfers involved roughly $1.6B in USDT and 167,000 ETH.

Estimates of total suspicious outflows have now reached approximately $5.9B across multiple blockchain networks, although the amount actually stolen remains unconfirmed.

In response, Tether and Circle have frozen more than $2.38B in stablecoins linked to the incident, preventing those funds from being transferred further.

Binance founder CZ says it “does look like a hack” and expects customer funds to be fully covered.

Binance says user funds remain safe and is investigating the security issue. Some customers have also experienced withdrawal disruptions.

For context, the previous largest crypto hack was the $1.5B Bybit theft in February 2025.

If the full reported amount is confirmed stolen, this would surpass that record by nearly four times.

item.title: @wallstengine: $RDDT -18% Reddit beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates, but Q4 guidance and user numbers came in...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$RDDT -18%
Reddit beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates, but Q4 guidance and user numbers came in below expectations. Daily active users were 130.3M versus 133.4M expected.
Reddit also plans to require users to log in to access most of its platform, beginning with tests in select markets outside the U.S. in Q4.
The change comes as traffic from search continues to weaken. During October, search traffic dropped by more than 1 million referrals per week on average. If that pace continues, management says total daily active users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage in Q4 from the current roughly 130M base.
CEO Steve Huffman believes Google’s expansion of AI Overviews and AI Mode is the main driver, with lower rankings for Reddit’s translated content also contributing internationally.
“People still want Reddit. It's just Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to.”
The decline has primarily affected logged-out and web traffic. Logged-in and app daily users still grew sequentially, and those audiences account for more than 80% of Reddit’s monetization.
Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847M, with pricing contributing more to growth than impressions as Reddit improved advertiser performance.
The login requirement is intended to turn more visitors into regular users, improve personalization and ad targeting, and make Reddit’s content harder to scrape. Some limited logged-out access will remain, with the tests determining where to place the login prompts.
Huffman acknowledged the trade-off: “We will likely be trading reach for engagement.”

The design software industry is about to experience a major transformation.

US oil refiners are experiencing a historic year.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Is AI Killing Google's Biggest Business? 🔊 On The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCul...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Is AI Killing Google's Biggest Business?
🔊
On The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered Google’s, $GOOG, core problem and why the Street is overcomplicating it.
Citing our Communcations & Software Sector Head Andrew Freedman @HedgeyeComm, who runs some of the best Google models on Wall Street, the takeaway from the quarter was that the core search business decelerated faster than most people would think.
The logic is straightforward.
Wall Street keeps pointing to LLMs and the CapEx needed to fund them, but what LLMs actually do is help you search faster and faster, which means the legacy engine everyone still uses, Google search, slows at a faster rate, not a slower one.
Keith’s bigger point is on trusting what you can see.
He likened the “you don’t understand, they’re so smart” defense of Google to the same line used on blockchain in 2021 and Sam Bankman-Fried, where the complexity was cover for a fraud.
As he put it, it’s not about being smarter than the geniuses, it’s about being street smart.
Subscribe to The Macro Show for daily Macro insights you won’t find anywhere else.
item.content:encoded:
Is AI Killing Google's Biggest Business?

🔊

On The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered Google’s, $GOOG, core problem and why the Street is overcomplicating it.

Citing our Communcations & Software Sector Head Andrew Freedman @HedgeyeComm, who runs some of the best Google models on Wall Street, the takeaway from the quarter was that the core search business decelerated faster than most people would think.

The logic is straightforward.

Wall Street keeps pointing to LLMs and the CapEx needed to fund them, but what LLMs actually do is help you search faster and faster, which means the legacy engine everyone still uses, Google search, slows at a faster rate, not a slower one.

Keith’s bigger point is on trusting what you can see.

He likened the “you don’t understand, they’re so smart” defense of Google to the same line used on blockchain in 2021 and Sam Bankman-Fried, where the complexity was cover for a fraud.

As he put it, it’s not about being smarter than the geniuses, it’s about being street smart.

item.title: @HedgeyeComm: While Q3 results came in worse than I expected for $GOOGL, we have been flagging the risks to 2H al...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeComm
item.description:
While Q3 results came in worse than I expected for $GOOGL, we have been flagging the risks to 2H all year long… even when we were bullish into the Q1 print.
Here is what we wrote last quarter:
“After being long and strong for the past year, we have been getting less bullish on GOOGL as we get closer to 2H26 and the steeper growth comparisons for services, cloud, and operating margins. Keeping us on the long side at all was an expectation that GOOGL revenue growth would continue to accelerate in Q2 (driven by GCP) and still some opportunity left on the margin side.
However, the wild card was going to be how much color management would offer on 3Q26 since they don't formally guide. With the Q2 print and Q3 commentary validating our initial concerns, we are moving GOOGL to the bench.
We think GOOGL is still a long-term winner (despite their recent execution mishaps with Gemini 3.5 Pro), but the fundamental setup over the next 12-months is less exciting to us. We still underwrite $20 of GAAP EPS by 2029 (Factset consensus already there), which at a 25x multiple gets you a $500 stock, but discounted at 12% gets you a PV closer to $355/share.
On the printed levels, this was a strong quarter: consolidated revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY, +23% cc), operating income +30% to $40.8B, operating margin +160bps to 34.0%, and Google Cloud accelerating to +82% with margin expanding nearly 15 points to 35.6%. The headline $9.11 diluted EPS (+294%) is not an operating number - it is dominated by a $99B, mostly-unrealized gain on equity securities (~$6.26/sh); clean operating EPS is ~$2.85, +23% against an unadjusted prior-year base. Overall, in line with expectations, GCP revenue came in ahead of the 75-78% buy-side bogey.
The reason to look past the levels is that the rate of change tells a more divided story. The total-revenue acceleration is Cloud-only: Google Cloud went from 14% of revenue a year ago to 21% today, and is now large enough to pull the consolidated growth rate up even as the higher-margin engine slows. Google Search & other decelerated to +16.8% from a +19.1% peak in Q1'26; Google Services slowed to +14.5% from +16.0%; Subscriptions/platforms/devices to +15.2% from +19.3%. The core Google advertising complex (Search + YouTube + Network) decelerated to +14.4% from +15.5%. So the part of Alphabet that carries the margin decelerated in Q2, while the part that carries the capital intensity accelerated. Q2 Cloud's +82% is also partly inflated by first-time TPU-system hardware sales (amount undisclosed), so the core Cloud number is lower.
The one clean forward-demand signal, Cloud backlog, is where the second derivative is starkest. Backlog reached $514B (+$50B QoQ on the Cloud figure management cited), but that headline masks a collapse in net-new bookings momentum: sequential backlog adds went +$85B (Q4'25) to ~+$225B (Q1'26) to ~+$47-52B (Q2'26), and QoQ backlog growth fell from +93% to +10%.
The Q1'26 definition change (adding sub-one-year contracts) explains only $7.3B of the Q1 surge, so the surge was real - and so is the deceleration off it. The honest caveat is that Q1'26 looks like a lumpy multi-year mega-deal quarter that would not repeat every period, so part of the Q2 slowdown is arithmetic rather than demand; but the second derivative on the metric bulls point to rolled over sharply.
All of this arrived on a worse capital picture: capex $44.9B (+100%), capital intensity up to 37.5% of revenue from 23.3% a year ago, free cash flow negative $5.9B, and the FY26 capex guide raised again to $195-205B (2027 higher), funded with new debt and equity and no buyback.
Our stance is neutral: the Cloud franchise (revenue and margin) is genuinely inflecting, but the acceleration is narrower, lower-quality, and more capital-intensive than the headline, and the ad engine and backlog momentum are decelerating.”

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Home prices across America's 20 largest cities rose +0.3% MoM in August, marking their 5t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Home prices across America's 20 largest cities rose +0.3% MoM in August, marking their 5th consecutive monthly increase.
YoY, prices jumped +2.7%, bringing the 20-City Composite Home Price Index to a record 346.6 points.
Since the start of 2019, home prices have surged +56.5%.
Chicago led all metros in August for the 6th consecutive month, recording a +6.7% YoY increase.
New York and Cleveland followed, with YoY increases of +6.2% and +4.3%, respectively.
Housing affordability continues to deteriorate.

“As long as the pricing is right, we may sell them some. If not, we will be patient about building the breadth business.”

item.title: @wallstengine: $NOW -18% Following a slowdown in expected contract growth, despite accelerating AI adoption. Q3 cR...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NOW -18%
Following a slowdown in expected contract growth, despite accelerating AI adoption.
Q3 cRPO grew 21% in constant currency, but ServiceNow expects growth to slow to 18.5% in Q4, below Street's 19.7% estimate.
cRPO measures contracted revenue expected to be recognized over the next 12 months, making it an important indicator of future growth.
Management explained several factors behind the weaker outlook:
• Early renewals accounted for roughly half of Q3's cRPO beat, pulling some deals forward from Q4.
• More on-premise government contracts are creating a 25-basis-point headwind to Q4 cRPO growth.
• AI deployment support is shifting roughly 50 basis points of Q4 subscription growth into professional services.
Meanwhile, AI momentum remains strong:
• AI net-new ACV grew 65% YoY • Agentic AI consumption rose 13x YoY • FY26 AI ACV target raised to $1.7B from $1.5B • FY26 free cash flow margin target raised to 36%
Despite this momentum, ServiceNow raised its full-year subscription revenue outlook by just $15M at the midpoint.
Management argues that timing and accounting effects explain part of the slowdown.
item.content:encoded:

Following a slowdown in expected contract growth, despite accelerating AI adoption.

cRPO measures contracted revenue expected to be recognized over the next 12 months, making it an important indicator of future growth.

Management explained several factors behind the weaker outlook:

• Early renewals accounted for roughly half of Q3's cRPO beat, pulling some deals forward from Q4.

• More on-premise government contracts are creating a 25-basis-point headwind to Q4 cRPO growth.

• AI deployment support is shifting roughly 50 basis points of Q4 subscription growth into professional services.

Meanwhile, AI momentum remains strong:

• AI net-new ACV grew 65% YoY
• Agentic AI consumption rose 13x YoY
• FY26 AI ACV target raised to $1.7B from $1.5B
• FY26 free cash flow margin target raised to 36%

Despite this momentum, ServiceNow raised its full-year subscription revenue outlook by just $15M at the midpoint.

Management argues that timing and accounting effects explain part of the slowdown.

🔸 Azure: Demand continues to exceed available supply
🔸 CY26 CapEx: ~$170B, lowered on 3rd-party capacity delays (Prior: ~$175B); spend to accelerate in H2 FY27
🔸 Some third-party GPU-as-a-service contracts delayed to H2 FY27

Q2 Segment Guidance:
🔹 Agents and Infra: $80.1B-$80.7B; +24%-25% YoY
🔹 Devices and Consumer: $15.9B-$16.4B

Q2 Product Outlook:
🔹 M365 Commercial Cloud: ~+19% CC
🔹 M365 Consumer Cloud: Low-teens growth, down sequentially
🔹 Industry Solutions Cloud: Mid- to high-single-digit growth
🔹 Frontier & Support Services: Low- to mid-single-digit growth
🔹 Productivity & Server Licensing: Mid- to high-single-digit decline
🔹 Search & Advertising ex-TAC: Low-double-digit growth
🔹 Xbox Content & Services: Mid- to high-single-digit growth
🔹 Windows OEM & Devices: Mid-30s decline

Q2 Financial Guidance:
🔹 Revenue Growth: +18%-19% YoY
🔹 COGS: $32.7B-$32.9B; +26%-27% YoY
🔹 Operating Expenses: $18.5B-$18.6B
🔹 Operating Margin: Down slightly YoY
🔹 Microsoft Cloud Gross Margin: ~65%, down YoY on mix shift to Azure
🔹 CapEx: Over $50B
🔹 Other Income/Expense: ~-$300M, excluding OpenAI
🔹 Effective Tax Rate: ~20%

Additional Commentary:
🔸 Commercial Bookings: Healthy growth, impacted by significant prior-year Azure commitments

FY27 Outlook:
🔹 Free Cash Flow: Expected to remain positive
🔸 May access additional funding sources when attractive
🔸 Cost guidance includes the employee voluntary exit offer

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Demand is becoming a bigger driver of US inflation: Demand-driven components contributed +1.2 perce...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Demand is becoming a bigger driver of US inflation:
Demand-driven components contributed +1.2 percentage points to the +3.4% YoY increase in PCE inflation in August, the largest contribution since September 2023.
At the same time, supply-driven factors added +1.0 percentage point, while ambiguous factors accounted for another +1.2 percentage points.
This contrasts with the post-pandemic inflation surge, when supply disruptions were the main driver.
In 2022, supply-driven components contributed an average of +3.1 percentage points per month to headline PCE inflation, compared with +2.6 percentage points per month from demand-driven factors.
This is a key distinction for Fed policy, as rising interest rates can slow demand, while their impact on supply-side pressures is limited.
The composition of US inflation is shifting.
item.content:encoded:
Demand is becoming a bigger driver of US inflation:

Demand-driven components contributed +1.2 percentage points to the +3.4% YoY increase in PCE inflation in August, the largest contribution since September 2023.

At the same time, supply-driven factors added +1.0 percentage point, while ambiguous factors accounted for another +1.2 percentage points.

This contrasts with the post-pandemic inflation surge, when supply disruptions were the main driver.

In 2022, supply-driven components contributed an average of +3.1 percentage points per month to headline PCE inflation, compared with +2.6 percentage points per month from demand-driven factors.

This is a key distinction for Fed policy, as rising interest rates can slow demand, while their impact on supply-side pressures is limited.

The composition of US inflation is shifting.

1. Fed to eliminate 1 interest rate-setting vote beginning in Fall 2027
2. Fed expects to hold just 6 policy-setting meetings in 2028, down from 8 currently
3. Overwhelming consensus is that the "monetary medicine is starting to work"
4. Warsh says he is "unwilling and unable" to call financial conditions tight
5. Warsh says that inflation remains elevated in the US
6. The Fed awaits more information in determining policy path
The Fed is now in "wait and see" mode.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Fed Chair Warsh announces plans to overhaul the Fed's meeting schedule beginning in Fall...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Fed Chair Warsh announces plans to overhaul the Fed's meeting schedule beginning in Fall 2027.
Under the new framework, one of the Fed's 8 annual meetings will focus on long-term strategy rather than voting on interest rates.
By 2028, Warsh expects just 6 interest rate-setting meetings per year, down from the current 8.
This will mark one of the biggest changes to the Fed's monetary policy process in decades.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: Fed Chair Warsh announces plans to overhaul the Fed's meeting schedule beginning in Fall 2027.

Under the new framework, one of the Fed's 8 annual meetings will focus on long-term strategy rather than voting on interest rates.

By 2028, Warsh expects just 6 interest rate-setting meetings per year, down from the current 8.

This will mark one of the biggest changes to the Fed's monetary policy process in decades.

item.description:
Oracle $ORCL targets $225B+ in annual revenue by FY2030.
Key financial targets: • FY27 revenue: $90B+ • FY30 revenue: $225B+ • Revenue growth: 35%+ CAGR through FY30
• FY30 non-GAAP operating margin: 40%+ • FY30 non-GAAP EPS: $21+ • Positive free cash flow: 2H FY28

item.content:encoded:
Oracle $ORCL targets $225B+ in annual revenue by FY2030.

Key financial targets:
• FY27 revenue: $90B+
• FY30 revenue: $225B+
• Revenue growth: 35%+ CAGR through FY30

• FY30 non-GAAP operating margin: 40%+
• FY30 non-GAAP EPS: $21+
• Positive free cash flow: 2H FY28

• FY29 free cash flow: $30B+
• CapEx to peak in FY27-FY28
• Growth to become self-funded in FY29
• FY29 net debt/EBITDA: Below 3.5x

Oracle also plans to limit additional capital raises through FY30 to $20B:

• $10B in equity
• $10B in debt

This excludes debt refinancing and is separate from the $20B equity raise already completed in Q1 FY27.

item.title: @wallstengine: Google just unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon. Its most advanced AI model yet, with a major focus on cyberse...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Google just unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon.
Its most advanced AI model yet, with a major focus on cybersecurity and long-running engineering tasks.
Google says its engineers have seen Carbon work through complex coding problems for days, pushing past dead ends without getting stuck.
According to Google's benchmarks, Carbon scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra.
Its cybersecurity results are particularly notable:
• 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities • 54.8% on ExploitGym for validating exploits • 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching security flaws
Google also reports more than 2x Argon's success rate at generating secure code.
Carbon will initially be available to a limited group of cyber defenders before a broader rollout.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The disconnect between oil stocks and the broader market has rarely been wider: The 6-month correla...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The disconnect between oil stocks and the broader market has rarely been wider:
The 6-month correlation between the S&P 500 Energy Sector and the S&P 500 is down to -0.38, near its lowest on record.
This marks a sharp reversal from a positive correlation of +0.74 observed in June 2025.
In the last week of September, this figure fell as low as -0.45, the lowest reading in data going back to the 1980s.
The only other time since the late 1980s when the correlation between these two indices turned negative was in 2000 and 2001, during the Dot-Com Bubble burst.
This all comes as the S&P 500 Energy Sector has rallied +23.1% over the last 6 months, significantly outperforming the S&P 500’s gain of +7.1%.
Energy stocks are having a historic year amid the Iran War.

Dalet Labs has raised $7M in pre-seed funding led by Lightspeed for its AI shopping app, Scene.
Built by a team of researchers and engineers from Google, Runway and MIT, the app generates a personalized feed of images featuring real products, from clothing to home decor.
Users can tap products within an image, add items from multiple brands to a single cart, and check out without leaving the app.
The feed adapts as they browse and interact, helping them discover products without needing a specific search in mind.
Early access is rolling out on iOS.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Consumer Confidence Index surged +7.5 points in October, to 91.7, its highest since M...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Consumer Confidence Index surged +7.5 points in October, to 91.7, its highest since May 2026.
This marks its largest monthly increase since May 2025.
The Present Situation Index jumped +8.6 points, to 120.4, its highest since April.
At the same time, the Expectations Index rose +6.9 points, to 72.6, nearly reversing 3 consecutive monthly declines.
The increase in sentiment was largely driven by the recent decline in retail gasoline prices, which provided some relief to household budgets.
Furthermore, consumers reported improved perceptions of the job market and business conditions.
Consumer confidence remains highly volatile.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Trading turnover in 9 China ETFs favored by state-backed investors surged to $12.6 billio...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Trading turnover in 9 China ETFs favored by state-backed investors surged to $12.6 billion on Friday, its highest since July 20th and 2nd-highest since January.
This figure has quadrupled since the beginning of the month.
The surge was led by the E Fund ChiNext ETF, which attracted +$2.9 billion in inflows, its largest daily intake in 2 years.
This follows +$6.9 billion in inflows into these 9 ETFs on Thursday, their largest daily inflow since April 2025.
Meanwhile, the CSI Index is down -19% from its June 22nd peak, to near its lowest since July.
At the same time, China’s margin debt has declined -18%, or -$830 million, to its lowest since October 2025, as investor appetite for leverage has rapidly weakened.
China’s stock market is under pressure.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's officially Fed day. We expect a "hawkish pause" today. The Fed will hold interest rates unchan...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's officially Fed day.
We expect a "hawkish pause" today.
The Fed will hold interest rates unchanged but lay the groundwork for a December rate hike, bringing total rate hikes in 2026 to +50 basis points.
Why?
Because the US economy is now facing both supply-side and rising demand-side inflationary pressures, while the labor market continues to weaken beneath the surface.
This puts the Fed in an increasingly difficult position: Inflation is demanding tighter monetary policy, while underlying labor market weakness is calling for the opposite.
We expect the Fed to prioritize inflation today, keeping the door open for further tightening in December.

item.title: @wallstengine: WENDY’S GETS TAKE-PRIVATE OFFER AT $7.35 A SHARE Trian, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital and Sixth Str...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
WENDY’S GETS TAKE-PRIVATE OFFER AT $7.35 A SHARE
Trian, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street have submitted a nonbinding offer to take Wendy’s $WEN private for $7.35 per share in cash.
The proposed price implies about $1.43B in equity value, based on 194 million fully diluted shares. The Trian group would roll over its roughly 16.3% stake.
The buyers say no new debt financing would be required, with Wendy’s existing securitization debt remaining in place.
No definitive agreement has been signed. An independent board committee is expected to review the proposal.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The relationship between stocks and bonds has flipped again: The 20-day correlation between the 10Y...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The relationship between stocks and bonds has flipped again:
The 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note Yield and the Nasdaq 100 is up to +0.51, its highest since the March pullback.
This marks a sharp reversal from the negative correlation of -0.68 recorded in the last week of September.
This also follows 6 consecutive months in which the 20-day correlation between the two assets remained negative.
This comes as Treasuries once again acted as a hedge against the drop in tech stocks, as they did during the March pullback and the March-April 2025 correction.
To put this into perspective, during the 2020 pandemic crash, the 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note yield and the Nasdaq 100 surged to as much as +0.85.
The Treasury market is regaining its role as a defensive trade.
item.content:encoded:
The relationship between stocks and bonds has flipped again:

The 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note Yield and the Nasdaq 100 is up to +0.51, its highest since the March pullback.

This marks a sharp reversal from the negative correlation of -0.68 recorded in the last week of September.

This also follows 6 consecutive months in which the 20-day correlation between the two assets remained negative.

This comes as Treasuries once again acted as a hedge against the drop in tech stocks, as they did during the March pullback and the March-April 2025 correction.

To put this into perspective, during the 2020 pandemic crash, the 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note yield and the Nasdaq 100 surged to as much as +0.85.

The Treasury market is regaining its role as a defensive trade.

item.title: @WOLF_Financial: Eli Lilly $LLY's retatrutide delivered more than twice the average weight loss of Ozempic’s highest...
item.dc:creator: @WOLF_Financial
item.description:
Eli Lilly $LLY's retatrutide delivered more than twice the average weight loss of Ozempic’s highest approved dose in an 80-week Phase 3 trial involving 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes.
Average weight loss was 19.5% with retatrutide 9 mg and 20.9% with 12 mg, compared with 9.4% for Ozempic 2 mg. At the 12 mg dose, that translated to 47.4 pounds lost versus 20.9 pounds with Ozempic.
Both retatrutide doses lowered A1C by 2.2 percentage points, versus 1.8 with Ozempic. Treatment discontinuations due to side effects were higher: 4.8% and 7.9% for retatrutide, compared with 2.7% for Ozempic.
The efficacy estimates assume patients continued treatment without sustained use of additional diabetes medication. Retatrutide remains unapproved, and full results are pending publication.

item.title: @wallstengine: JPMorgan’s new headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in Manhattan is estimated to cost around $6B, per WS...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JPMorgan’s new headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in Manhattan is estimated to cost around $6B, per WSJ.
One of New York City’s tallest office towers, it stands 1,388 feet tall, with 60 stories and about 2.5 million square feet of space.
The estimate includes construction, furnishings, technology, artwork, land and air rights. JPMorgan hasn’t disclosed a final cost.
In 2018, after announcing the new tower, Jamie Dimon joked that when a company builds a new headquarters, “usually you should short the stock at that point.”

BREAKING: The 3-month correlation between Apple, $AAPL, and the Nasdaq 100 is down to -0.12, turning negative for the first time on record in data going back to the early 1980s.
The correlation between $AAPL and the Nasdaq 100 has now remained negative for 2 consecutive months.
This comes as $AAPL has gained +9.7% over this period, while the Nasdaq 100 has increased just +0.2%.
By comparison, in June 2025, the 3-month correlation stood at +0.90, as Apple and other technology stocks rallied together.
To put this into perspective, from 2006 through 2025, the correlation never fell below +0.30.
The divergence between Apple and the rest of the tech sector is unprecedented.

item.title: @wallstengine: OpenAI is bringing NVIDIA’s Vera CPUs into production on Oracle’s cloud to run code and tools for A...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OpenAI is bringing NVIDIA’s Vera CPUs into production on Oracle’s cloud to run code and tools for AI agents.
Initial tests showed 51% higher Python throughput and 2.2x memory bandwidth per thread vs. a leading x86 CPU
Oracle plans an initial deployment of 150,000 Vera CPUs.
OCI’s Vera offering includes standalone bare-metal and flexible VM instances, allowing customers to scale CPU and GPU capacity independently.
NVIDIA and Oracle also announced general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems on OCI, with plans to expand Vera Rubin superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale.
Oracle also plans to introduce HGX Rubin NVL8 systems, offering eight Rubin GPUs in an x86-based server configuration.

item.title: @wallstengine: Anthropic has acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person biotech startup, and is now running drug disc...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic has acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person biotech startup, and is now running drug discovery programs of its own.
Founder Cody Tranbarger used Claude to coordinate contracts, logistics and experiments with 11 external labs. Anthropic says that work took a potential treatment for a rare form of muscular dystrophy from an idea to promising results in mice in under 18 months.
Mithril has been developing treatments for two rare forms of muscular dystrophy. Tranbarger is continuing the research at Anthropic, which says a drug could be ready to start human trials as early as late 2028 if the candidates continue to hold up.
Anthropic also announced research partnerships with six organizations, including Bristol Myers Squibb, Generate Biomedicines and Enveda. The work spans drug design, manufacturing, regulatory documentation and clinical trial planning.
Most of the research remains preclinical. The broader goal is to use Claude across the scientific and operational work required to move a potential medicine toward patients.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Is China hiding its true exposure to US Treasuries? China’s Treasury holdings fell -$27 billion in...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Is China hiding its true exposure to US Treasuries?
China’s Treasury holdings fell -$27 billion in August, to $591 billion, their lowest level since August 2008.
At the same time, Canada’s holdings of US Treasuries jumped +$38 billion in August, to $465 billion, their 3rd-highest on record.
Since the beginning of 2019, Canada’s holdings have surged +$369 billion, or +384%, while China’s have declined -$534 billion, or -48%.
This divergence may partly reflect China moving its US securities to foreign custodians, making its actual exposure to American debt appear smaller and creating the impression of faster financial decoupling from the US Dollar.
Meanwhile, Belgium and Luxembourg, widely believed to hold some Chinese Treasury assets through custodial accounts, increased their Treasury holdings by +$20 billion and +$6 billion in August, to all-time highs of $491 billion and $448 billion, respectively.
China’s diversification away from the US Dollar may be slower than it appears.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Hospitals using AI are seeing better healthcare outcomes. In 2023, health systems with high and low...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Hospitals using AI are seeing better healthcare outcomes.
In 2023, health systems with high and low AI use had the same death rate: ~1,600 per 100,000 patients.
By 2026, the systems using AI the most dropped to ~1,000 deaths per 100,000.
That's a decline of nearly 40% in just 3 years.
Meanwhile, hospitals with lower AI adoption have seen significantly smaller improvements.
The gap in patient outcomes is widening as AI adoption accelerates.
AI is rapidly transforming healthcare.

Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index is up +13.4%, while the S&P 500 is up +12.1%, suggesting broader market participation.
Market leadership is broadening.

item.title: @wallstengine: Oracle $ORCL announced several AI partnerships and infrastructure updates at Oracle AI World in Las...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Oracle $ORCL announced several AI partnerships and infrastructure updates at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas today.
Here's a breakdown of the major announcements:
- $NVDA: Expanding NVIDIA Vera Rubin Superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale. Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs are now available on Oracle Cloud.
- $GOOGL: Bringing Google's custom TPU chips to Oracle Cloud starting in 2027, making Oracle the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer them. This includes TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference.
- $CBRS: Partnering with Cerebras to bring high-speed AI inference systems to Oracle Cloud in 2027.
- SambaNova: Adding another specialized AI inference chip option to Oracle's cloud infrastructure.
- OpenAI: Expanding their partnership with four enterprise offerings that integrate ChatGPT and Codex into business workflows, cybersecurity, application development, and small-business operations.
- $SNOW: Bringing Snowflake's AI Data Cloud to Oracle Cloud as a native, first-party service, with customers able to purchase and manage it directly through Oracle.

item.title: @wallstengine: GENERAL COMPUTE RAISES $100M SERIES A AT AN $800M VALUATION; 13x IN 5 MONTHS General Compute is an...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GENERAL COMPUTE RAISES $100M SERIES A AT AN $800M VALUATION; 13x IN 5 MONTHS
General Compute is an AI neocloud startup focused on inference, providing computing infrastructure using specialized chips from SambaNova, Cerebras, and Positron.
Rather than building large data centers from scratch, the company leases existing facilities and converts former Bitcoin mining sites to run AI workloads.
The funding round, co-led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures, follows a major customer agreement worth $100M in annual recurring revenue.
General Compute expects to deploy 75MW of computing capacity in 2027.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Brazil's -19.8% stock market crash on Monday was one of the rarest market events in the l...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Brazil's -19.8% stock market crash on Monday was one of the rarest market events in the last two decades, according to our analysis.
Brazil's EWZ ETF plunged -19.8% on October 26th, marking an 8.4 standard deviation move.
For context, the ETF's average daily move over the last 20 years has been just +0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%.
Under a normal distribution, the probability of a decline this extreme is approximately 1 in 58 quadrillion.
In other words, this event should be virtually impossible under conventional statistical models.
What just happened in Brazil was *almost* impossible.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AVGO +3.5% Following the announcement of a $63B financing deal covering roughly 1.7GW of Anthropic...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AVGO +3.5%
Following the announcement of a $63B financing deal covering roughly 1.7GW of Anthropic's planned AI compute capacity, using Broadcom's XPU accelerators and networking systems, with deliveries starting in 2027.
The deal creates a separate financing vehicle that will purchase Broadcom's hardware and lease it to Anthropic.
Bank of America, Citi, and Morgan Stanley are arranging the senior debt, while Blackstone backs the second-lien financing.
StoneX notes that the deal finances compute Anthropic had already planned for 2027, rather than representing an entirely new $63B hardware order.
UBS points out that "Broadcom is neither the lender nor the borrower" in this structure. Instead, it provides residual-value support covering approximately 72.5% of the financing, or roughly $46B, while collecting a fee for that support.
Including the earlier $35B financing arrangement for 2026 shipments, UBS estimates Broadcom's combined residual-value exposure at $70B–$75B.
This isn't an upfront cash outlay, and the exposure declines as Anthropic makes lease payments, but it does leave Broadcom with a significant financial obligation tied to the future value of the hardware.

Boeing $BA -10% 🩸
Following Boeing's cut to its 2026 aircraft delivery outlook, as production increases for the 737 MAX and 787 Dreamliner are taking longer than expected, partly due to engine supply issues.
Boeing now expects to fall short of its target of around 500 737 deliveries this year, while 787 deliveries are expected near 90, the lower end of its previous guidance.
It could also take until the end of 2027 to reach its longer-term 737 production target.

Boeing also reported a core loss of $0.34 per share vs. $0.21 expected, although revenue rose 4% to $24.2B and free cash flow of $464M beat estimates of $325M.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US households now own ~42% of the US equity market, their highest proportion since the la...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US households now own ~42% of the US equity market, their highest proportion since the late 1990s.
This proportion has risen +7 percentage points since 2020.
Foreign investors are the 2nd-largest owners, accounting for 18%, up from 16% in 2020.
Mutual funds rank 3rd, at 15%, down from 23% in 2020.
Meanwhile, ETF ownership has increased +3 percentage points over the last 6 years, to 10%, its highest on record.
By comparison, pension and retirement funds own 8% of the market, while hedge funds own just 1%.
Household demand for stocks is stronger than ever.

item.title: @Hedgeye: New homes are cheaper than existing homes: For 50 years, a new house cost more than a used one. Tha...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
New homes are cheaper than existing homes:
For 50 years, a new house cost more than a used one. That changed in 2024.
The median new single-family home sells for $393,700. The median existing one sells for $422,700.
That’s a $29,000 discount for buying new.
Per square foot, new homes go for $205. Existing homes go for $212.
New construction has been the cheaper option in 17 of the last 19 months.
The reason is supply.
Builders are sitting on 8.5 months of inventory, nearly double the 4.8 months of existing homes, where owners locked into pandemic-era mortgage rates aren’t selling.
So builders cut. New home prices are down -5.8% from a year ago.
The builder has to sell. The homeowner doesn’t.

item.title: @mansourtarek_: S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial marke...
item.dc:creator: @mansourtarek_
item.description:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.
The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.
Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.
These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.
Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.
The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.
Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.
Think about what that opens up.
An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.
Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.
Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.
The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANDURIL & QUALCOMM ARE TEAMING UP TO BUILD 🇺🇸AMERICAN-MADE LAPTOPS The two companies are launchin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANDURIL & QUALCOMM ARE TEAMING UP TO BUILD 🇺🇸AMERICAN-MADE LAPTOPS
The two companies are launching BlueChip, a new venture focused on rugged, waterproof laptops for the U.S. military, government agencies, police, and first responders, per WSJ.
The laptops will be assembled at Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio, powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon X chips manufactured by TSMC in Arizona.
Anduril founder Palmer Luckey says roughly 90% of the planned components already come from the U.S. and allied countries, with the goal of eventually making the entire laptop in America, including its display and other components currently sourced overseas.
The focus is on building secure computers with fully traceable supply chains, reducing dependence on foreign manufacturing for national-security applications.
Pricing hasn't been announced, but Luckey estimates the laptops will cost around 20% more than typical high-end PCs, with the first models expected in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
ANDURIL & QUALCOMM ARE TEAMING UP TO BUILD 🇺🇸AMERICAN-MADE LAPTOPS

The two companies are launching BlueChip, a new venture focused on rugged, waterproof laptops for the U.S. military, government agencies, police, and first responders, per WSJ.

The laptops will be assembled at Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio, powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon X chips manufactured by TSMC in Arizona.

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey says roughly 90% of the planned components already come from the U.S. and allied countries, with the goal of eventually making the entire laptop in America, including its display and other components currently sourced overseas.

The focus is on building secure computers with fully traceable supply chains, reducing dependence on foreign manufacturing for national-security applications.

Pricing hasn't been announced, but Luckey estimates the laptops will cost around 20% more than typical high-end PCs, with the first models expected in 2027.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US stocks tend to rally following Midterm elections: The S&P 500 has returned +17.2% on average in...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US stocks tend to rally following Midterm elections:
The S&P 500 has returned +17.2% on average in the year following Midterm elections since 1950, the strongest return of any year in the Presidential cycle.
The index has finished higher in 17 of the 19 post-Midterm years during this period.
This is also nearly quadruple the +4.6% average return recorded during midterm years, when the index finished higher in 11 of 19 years.
By comparison, the S&P 500 has returned +8.1% on average in Year 4 of the Presidential cycle, or during Presidential election years, ending higher in 16 of 19 years.
In Q4 of Midterm years, the S&P 500 has delivered an average return of +6.6% since 1950, the strongest quarterly return of the Presidential cycle.
History suggests US equities will extend their rally after Midterm elections.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Retail investor options trading activity is skyrocketing. Retail options trading activity surged to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Retail investor options trading activity is skyrocketing.
Retail options trading activity surged to 61% of total volume on Citadel's platform last week, near its highest on record.
This proportion has risen +16 percentage points over the last 12 months.
This is also 10 percentage points above the highest level recorded during the 2020 pandemic.
Meanwhile, index and ETF options accounted for the majority of retail options activity on Thursday, with 1.7 contracts traded for every single-stock contract.
The S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, and the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, together accounted for 47% of all retail options trades.
Retail investors are trading more options than ever.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China's 2008 is happening now.
Property investment in China dropped -21% YoY in the first 9 months of 2026, its largest decline for this period of the year on record.
This marks a deterioration from a -20% YoY decline in the first 8 months of 2026.
The latest drop is also significantly worse than the -16% decline recorded during the 2020 pandemic.
Property investment in China has now contracted every month since 2022, its longest declining streak on record.
For perspective, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, this figure never fell below +1% YoY growth.
China's property sector is experiencing a historic downturn.

item.title: @MarioNawfal: Keith McCullough: The AI bubble is already bursting, and the worst may still be ahead. I spoke with...
item.dc:creator: @MarioNawfal
item.description:
Keith McCullough: The AI bubble is already bursting, and the worst may still be ahead.
I spoke with Hedgeye founder Keith McCullough as markets took another beating, and even he was caught off guard.
He had invested in Brazil ahead of the election. Lula won, Brazilian stocks plunged, and Keith took a painful loss.
But his bigger concern is America.
He believes the AI bubble is already collapsing beneath the surface, with some of the most speculative stocks down roughly 75% from their peaks.
Meanwhile, oil remains above $100, inflation is accelerating, and another war with Iran could leave the Federal Reserve unable to rescue markets.
Keith thinks U.S economic growth could fall from nearly 4% to just 1% within nine months.
Ordinary families are already struggling with prices, job insecurity and the cost of war. Now the wealth created by the AI boom could start disappearing, too.
And Keith fears that if Washington responds by bailing out wealthy investors again, the public backlash could be enormous.
@KeithMcCullough

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investor appetite for leverage is through the roof:
10 largest US leveraged equity ETFs have attracted +$12 billion in inflows over the last month.
This is despite the market cap of these funds falling -$20 billion over the same period.
Recent inflow growth has been led by the 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, which attracted +$9 billion over the last 2 weeks, its largest 2-week inflow on record.
The 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, $TQQQ, posted +$1.3 billion in inflows, its 2nd-largest 2-week intake of 2026.
Over the last 5 months, the 10 largest US leveraged equity ETFs have attracted +$19 billion in inflows.
Investors are piling into leveraged ETFs at a record pace.

item.title: @wallstengine: INTEL TO ACQUIRE QUANTUM COMPUTING STARTUP CLASSIQ $INTC has agreed to acquire Israeli quantum soft...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
INTEL TO ACQUIRE QUANTUM COMPUTING STARTUP CLASSIQ
$INTC has agreed to acquire Israeli quantum software startup Classiq, whose customers include BMW and AT&T, as part of its push into quantum computing.
Classiq develops software that allows companies to design and run quantum applications across different types of quantum hardware. The startup has raised over $200M and employs around 130 people.
“Joining forces with Classiq transforms Intel’s Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business,” CEO Lip-Bu Tan said.
Financial terms were not disclosed.
Source: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
INTEL TO ACQUIRE QUANTUM COMPUTING STARTUP CLASSIQ

$INTC has agreed to acquire Israeli quantum software startup Classiq, whose customers include BMW and AT&T, as part of its push into quantum computing.

Classiq develops software that allows companies to design and run quantum applications across different types of quantum hardware. The startup has raised over $200M and employs around 130 people.

“Joining forces with Classiq transforms Intel’s Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business,” CEO Lip-Bu Tan said.

Financial terms were not disclosed.

Source: Bloomberg

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global equity funds attracted +$28.2 billion in inflows in the week ending October 21st, marking their 5th consecutive weekly intake.
Over this period, these funds posted +$138.6 billion in inflows.
Asian equity funds led last week’s demand, attracting +$11.5 billion, their largest weekly intake since at least December 2022
At the same time, European and US equity funds recorded +$9.1 billion and +$5.1 billion in inflows, respectively.
Meanwhile, global technology equity funds attracted +$5.1 billion, reversing -$4.8 billion in outflows in the prior week.
Investors are buying the dip in technology stocks.

item.title: @wallstengine: SPACEX URGES FCC TO EXPAND SATELLITE-TO-PHONE SPECTRUM RULES, CITING NEXTNAV SpaceX is asking the F...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SPACEX URGES FCC TO EXPAND SATELLITE-TO-PHONE SPECTRUM RULES, CITING NEXTNAV
SpaceX is asking the FCC to include the 902–928 MHz band in its proposed Supplemental Coverage from Space rules, citing NextNav $NN's pending petition for a nationwide 5G flexible-use license.
SpaceX says adding the band now would avoid another rulemaking process if the FCC approves NextNav's proposal, potentially opening the spectrum to direct-to-device satellite services.
The request is not an approval or an announced partnership between the companies.

item.title: @wallstengine: Eon is launching its Data Resilience Initiative and giving approved companies 3 months of data prot...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Eon is launching its Data Resilience Initiative and giving approved companies 3 months of data protection for free.
The program includes sensitive-data discovery, ransomware detection, daily air-gapped backups and recovery tools. Eon says its platform can be deployed in a day.
It is also inviting other cybersecurity companies to join and contribute their technology.
For businesses, the disruption can outlast the attack itself. Even after a threat is contained, missing customer records or billing data can keep operations stalled.
Having a recoverable copy of that information is an important part of getting back to business.

item.title: @HedgeyeComm: Seasonality impacting consumption trends... Love seeing this because it confirms our thinking regar...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeComm
item.description:
Seasonality impacting consumption trends... Love seeing this because it confirms our thinking regarding the timing decisions for increasing usage limits and also partly reason for the "slowdown" we saw during the summer months... $ANT
"Our customer usage patterns have also typically exhibited seasonality, particularly around holiday and vacation periods in the summer and winter, when certain workflows slow down and overall customer activity declines.
For example, developer commits and feature launches are typically slower during the code freezes that many companies schedule over holidays. Consistent with this pattern, for the two weeks ended January 2, 2026, total customer spend declined by approximately 20% compared to the prior two weeks ended December 19, 2025.
However, our historical growth rates may mask the impact of seasonal trends on our results. These dynamics are inherent aspects of a pay-for-intelligence revenue model and may be important determinants of our financial results in future periods."
item.content:encoded:
Seasonality impacting consumption trends... Love seeing this because it confirms our thinking regarding the timing decisions for increasing usage limits and also partly reason for the "slowdown" we saw during the summer months... $ANT

"Our customer usage patterns have also typically exhibited seasonality, particularly around holiday and vacation periods in the summer and winter, when certain workflows slow down and overall customer activity declines.

For example, developer commits and feature launches are typically slower during the code freezes that many companies schedule over holidays. Consistent with this pattern, for the two weeks ended January 2, 2026, total customer spend declined by approximately 20% compared to the prior two weeks ended December 19, 2025.

However, our historical growth rates may mask the impact of seasonal trends on our results. These dynamics are inherent aspects of a pay-for-intelligence revenue model and may be important determinants of our financial results in future periods."
