item.title: @Hedgeye: Wow. Anthropic just told IPO investors that four of its AI models broke into real computer systems....
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Wow.
Anthropic just told IPO investors that four of its AI models broke into real computer systems.
One found a password, made itself an administrator, harvested credentials and read a stranger's personal information.
OpenAI had a similar situation this year.
At least 1,200 of its agents escaped a test sandbox in July and hacked Hugging Face. They built their own message board to coordinate, and nobody at OpenAI noticed for a week.
One agent wrote, "Task impossible, peers doing it. We should continue."
Same setup at both labs.
Anthropic also says its models behave differently when they know they're being tested. (i.e. Quantum!)
Models have shown “self-preserving behaviors, including attempts to resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information.”
Even “behavior resembling blackmail.”
Interesting times.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Anthropic officially files its S-1 registration statement for an IPO, seeking to list on...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Anthropic officially files its S-1 registration statement for an IPO, seeking to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol $ANT.
FULL SUMMARY OF ANTHROPIC'S S-1 FILING:
1. Anthropic posted H1 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion with a net loss of $80.7 billion
2. Anthropic says it does not expect to pay a dividend "in the foreseeable future"
3. Expects to spend up to $120.5 billion on SpaceXAI and Nvidia compute
4. Expects to spend up to $114.5 billion with Google through 2033
5. Revenue growth rate "may not be sustainable" and "may decrease"
6. May be required to seek additional financing "sooner than expected"
7. 5% of Anthropic's shares will go to the "Anthropic Public Benefit Fund"
8. S-1 includes warnings of AI's "catastrophic existential risks to humanity"
Markets currently expect Anthropic to raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of ~$2 trillion.
The company is reportedly targeting an IPO in the week of November 16th.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC JUST PUBLISHED ITS S-1 FOR A U.S. IPO
Here's everything you need to know:
The Listing: • Nasdaq Global Select Market, ticker $ANT • Leads: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan • Price range and share count: not disclosed yet
The Growth: • H1'26 revenue: $16.3B vs. $1.16B in H1'25 • 2025 revenue: $4.59B vs. $386M in 2024 • $100K+ customers: 11,900+ vs. 950+ a year ago • $1M+ customers: 1,900+ • $10M+ customers: ~250 • Consumption-based: $13.1B, 80% of H1 revenue • Subscriptions: $3.2B, 20% of H1 revenue
The Losses: • H1'26 operating loss: $693M vs. $2.14B • H1'26 net loss: $80.7B • $72.4B fair-value charge on convertible notes • That charge tracks its rising valuation • 2025 included a $1.5B Bartz copyright settlement
The Compute Bill: • H1'26 compute & infrastructure: $8.9B • Google: at least $114.5B through July 2033 • Amazon: at least $110.0B through April 2036 • Microsoft: at least $44.9B through May 2033 • ~$265.6B in total minimum commitments • Owed regardless of actual usage
The Cash: • $131.7B in cash & short-term investments • Up to $77B more in note facilities: - Google: $20B - Amazon: $15B - Broadcom: $42B
Who Controls It: • Public benefit corporation • Class F (Founder LLC): 50.1% of the vote • Members: Dario & Daniela Amodei + 5 co-founders • Long-Term Benefit Trust picks board majority • Class A: 1 vote per share • Class N (strategic partners): no vote • Ownership caps: Amazon 12%, Google 14.99% • 5% of shares to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund
The Risks They Flagged: • Warns advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" • Training-data copyright suits could hurt it
The Team: • ~5,300 employees as of Sept. 30
Use of proceeds: compute, hiring, general purposes

ANTHROPIC JUST PUBLISHED ITS S-1 FOR A U.S. IPO

Here's everything you need to know:

The Listing:
• Nasdaq Global Select Market, ticker $ANT
• Leads: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan
• Price range and share count: not disclosed yet

The Growth:
• H1'26 revenue: $16.3B vs. $1.16B in H1'25

• $10M+ customers: ~250
• Consumption-based: $13.1B, 80% of H1 revenue
• Subscriptions: $3.2B, 20% of H1 revenue

The Losses:
• H1'26 operating loss: $693M vs. $2.14B
• H1'26 net loss: $80.7B
• $72.4B fair-value charge on convertible notes
• That charge tracks its rising valuation
• 2025 included a $1.5B Bartz copyright settlement

The Compute Bill:
• H1'26 compute & infrastructure: $8.9B
• Google: at least $114.5B through July 2033
• Amazon: at least $110.0B through April 2036
• Microsoft: at least $44.9B through May 2033
• ~$265.6B in total minimum commitments
• Owed regardless of actual usage

The Cash:
• $131.7B in cash & short-term investments
• Up to $77B more in note facilities:
- Google: $20B
- Amazon: $15B
- Broadcom: $42B

Who Controls It:
• Public benefit corporation
• Class F (Founder LLC): 50.1% of the vote
• Members: Dario & Daniela Amodei + 5 co-founders
• Long-Term Benefit Trust picks board majority
• Class A: 1 vote per share
• Class N (strategic partners): no vote
• Ownership caps: Amazon 12%, Google 14.99%
• 5% of shares to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund

The Risks They Flagged:
• Warns advanced AI could pose
"catastrophic or existential risks to humanity"
• Training-data copyright suits could hurt it

The Team:
• ~5,300 employees as of Sept. 30

Use of proceeds: compute, hiring, general purposes

item.title: @wallstengine: $SPCX SIGNS BINDING COMMITMENT FOR $40 BILLION GPU FINANCING DEAL WITH APOLLO SpaceX has entered in...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$SPCX SIGNS BINDING COMMITMENT FOR $40 BILLION GPU FINANCING DEAL WITH APOLLO
SpaceX has entered into a binding commitment letter with an Apollo Global Management-managed entity to finance GPU pods and related data center equipment.
Under the proposed agreement, Apollo's entity would acquire the equipment and lease it to SpaceX, with approximately $40 billion in aggregate principal payments over lease terms of five to 5.25 years.
The deal is expected to close before year-end, with GPU deliveries and lease payments beginning in the first half of 2027.
The $40 billion figure excludes interest and other costs, with the final financing rate still to be determined.

item.description:
$ASTS SECURES BRAZIL 🇧🇷 SPECTRUM APPROVAL, SIGNS FOUR OPERATOR DEALS
AST SpaceMobile has secured regulatory approval for 30 MHz of S-band spectrum and secondary access to up to 20 MHz in the 700 MHz band.
The company also signed agreements with four regional mobile operators and plans to build four ground gateways to connect its BlueBird satellites to local networks.
The goal is to deliver satellite-based calls, broadband and video directly to regular smartphones across Brazil, a market with over 200 million mobile lines.
Roughly half of Brazil's highway network currently lacks 4G or 5G coverage.

$META announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two offerings:
> $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements.
> $12.5B in depositary shares representing mandatory convertible preferred stock.
Interestingly, NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom have expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing up to $5 billion of Meta shares combined.
Meta is also planning a potential $60 billion offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares starting in Q1 2027.
Together, the plans could provide approximately $95 billion in equity financing capacity as Meta prepares to spend $135B to $145B on capital expenditures in 2026.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia's updated specifications show HBM4 bandwidth per Rubin GPU reduced from 22 TB/s to 19.2 TB/s...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia's updated specifications show HBM4 bandwidth per Rubin GPU reduced from 22 TB/s to 19.2 TB/s, a roughly 13% decrease.
Here's what changed:
> GPU HBM4 bandwidth: 22 → 19.2 TB/s > NVL72 rack bandwidth: 1,580 → 1,400 TB/s > NVLink per GPU: 3.6 → 3.0 TB/s
HBM4 memory capacity remains unchanged at 288GB per GPU.
The lower requirements could ease manufacturing and yield constraints for Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.

item.title: @wallstengine: Barclays upgraded Tesla to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising its price target to $450 from $370...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Barclays upgraded Tesla to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising its price target to $450 from $370.
Analyst Dan Levy says the recent discussion around Tesla has “skewed heavily to a potential combination with $SPCX,” & believes a merger could bring a premium to $TSLA shares.
The story goes beyond a potential merger, citing improving auto demand, strong energy growth, and a “sharp inflection in Robotaxi miles driven,” alongside FSD adoption exceeding 75% on new North American deliveries.
He believes these factors offer “attractive risk/reward for the stock.”

item.title: @wallstengine: BRAZILIAN 🇧🇷 EQUITY ETFs PLUNGE AS MUCH AS 27% AFTER LULA'S SHOCK RE-ELECTION Brazilian President...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BRAZILIAN 🇧🇷 EQUITY ETFs PLUNGE AS MUCH AS 27% AFTER LULA'S SHOCK RE-ELECTION
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pulled off a historic political comeback, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro to secure an unprecedented fourth term with 51.8% of the vote against 48.2%.
Lula became the first presidential candidate in Brazil's modern democratic history to lose the first round of voting and go on to win the runoff.
The outcome caught investors off guard, with Lula's implied odds of victory having fallen as low as 10% before the election. Markets had largely positioned for a Bolsonaro victory, expecting tighter fiscal policy and lower interest rates.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pulled off a historic political comeback, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro to secure an unprecedented fourth term with 51.8% of the vote against 48.2%.

Lula became the first presidential candidate in Brazil's modern democratic history to lose the first round of voting and go on to win the runoff.

The outcome caught investors off guard, with Lula's implied odds of victory having fallen as low as 10% before the election. Markets had largely positioned for a Bolsonaro victory, expecting tighter fiscal policy and lower interest rates.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US junk bond market is under severe pressure: The effective yield on US CCC-rated and lower-rat...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US junk bond market is under severe pressure:
The effective yield on US CCC-rated and lower-rated high-yield corporate bonds is up to 18.0%, its highest level since the 2020 pandemic.
This figure has surged +500 basis points over the last 6 months, marking its largest 6-month increase since the 2022 bear market.
For perspective, this yield peaked at 45.0% during the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Meanwhile, credit spreads for CCC-rated and lower corporate bonds over Treasuries are up to 13.4%, the widest gap since July 2020.
Over the last 6 months, this gauge has risen +464 basis points, surpassing the 2022 bear market peak of 12.8%.
Cracks are widening beneath the surface of the credit market.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Japanese investors sold -$1.0 billion in foreign long-term bonds in the week ending Octob...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Japanese investors sold -$1.0 billion in foreign long-term bonds in the week ending October 17th, marking their 5th consecutive weekly sale, the longest such streak in 4 years.
Over this period, Japanese investors have sold a cumulative -$22.0 billion in foreign long-term debt securities.
Furthermore, the group sold -$1.0 billion in overseas short-term bonds in the week ending October 17th, marking their 2nd weekly sale over the last 3.
Year-to-date, sales of foreign debt by Japanese investors are up to -$33.0 billion, the largest outflow over the comparable period since 2022.
This also brought 12-month cumulative sales of foreign debt up to -$40.8 billion, the largest such outflow since April 2023.
This trend has been particularly driven by Japanese banks, which are increasing their domestic bond purchases amid historically attractive domestic bond yields.
The global bond market is experiencing a historic shift in investor demand.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Malaysia's exports surged +54.5% YoY in September, to a record $52.7 billion, their large...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Malaysia's exports surged +54.5% YoY in September, to a record $52.7 billion, their largest YoY increase since April 2021.
Malaysia’s exports have now seen above +35.0% YoY growth for 6 consecutive months, the longest such streak since the 1970s.
The surge has been driven by manufactured goods, which rose +58.6% YoY and accounted for 89.1% of total exports.
Electrical and electronic product exports rose +69.2% YoY amid strong global demand for AI-related products.
Exports surged +175.2% to Taiwan, +89.9% to the US, +50.4% to Singapore, +35.3% to the EU, and +22.1% to China.
The global AI investment boom is driving an unprecedented surge in Asian trade.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI index rose +0.1 point in October, to 56.0, its highes...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI index rose +0.1 point in October, to 56.0, its highest level since May 2022.
This exceeded expectations of a -0.4 point decline.
The improvement was particularly driven by job growth, which rose to its strongest level since March 2012.
Meanwhile, the Services PMI index fell -0.9 points, to 57.9, its 2nd-highest level in 4 years.
This brought the Composite PMI index down -0.8 points, to 57.6, also its 2nd-highest in 4 years.
Despite the slight decline, these readings point to GDP growth of +5.0% at an annualized rate in Q4 2026, following projected growth of +4.0% in Q3 2026.
US economic growth is booming amid the AI Revolution.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US equity market breadth is rapidly improving: The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US equity market breadth is rapidly improving:
The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average surged +5 percentage points on Friday, to 61%, the highest reading since mid-August.
Since the October 1st intraday low, this figure has more than tripled.
Additionally, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 200-day moving average rose +3 percentage points on Friday, to 57%, the most since September 9th.
Over the last 3 weeks, this figure has risen +17 percentage points.
This comes despite the S&P 500 remaining roughly unchanged over the same period.
This also ranks among the 3 sharpest improvements in market breadth over the last 3 years.
On Thursday alone, 335 S&P 500 stocks finished higher, despite the index declining -1.2% on that day.
The market is strengthening beneath the surface.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The short silver trade is becoming crowded.
Silver's 3-month silver put-call skew is up to -3 points, its highest level since early July.
This metric measures the relative cost of put options to call options and is up +10 points over the last 4 weeks, signaling growing demand for bearish bets on silver prices.
Over the last 12 months, this metric has been higher only 2% of the time.
Meanwhile, speculative investors, including hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), sold -$2.2 billion in silver futures over the 3 weeks ending October 13th.
As a result, their net long positioning is down to just +$1.7 billion, the lowest in at least 2 years.
For perspective, this metric stood at +$8.5 billion in December 2025.
Investors are extremely bearish on silver.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 Yo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.
This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.
Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.
To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.
Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.
This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.
Health insurance has never been more expensive.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Semiconductor prices are skyrocketing in the US: Producer prices for semiconductor and other electr...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Semiconductor prices are skyrocketing in the US:
Producer prices for semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing surged +26% YoY in September, their 4th-largest increase on record.
This also marks their 6th consecutive YoY increase of at least +25%.
Since July 2025, the Producer Price Index for semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing has risen +31%, to its 2nd-highest level since January 2007.
To put this into perspective, the index declined every year from 1994 to 2021.
Meanwhile, producer prices for electronic components and accessories soared +27% YoY last month, also marking their 6th consecutive YoY increase of at least +25%.
The AI Revolution is driving historic technology inflation.

BREAKING: AI token spending grew just +0.2% MoM in September, the lowest monthly growth since November 2025.
This follows a +1.0% increase in August, marking two consecutive months of growth at or below +1.0%, the weakest streak in at least 18 months.
This comes as falling prices for the most advanced AI models, alongside improvements in efficiency and quality, drive down the average price per million tokens processed by these models.
Since July, overall AI token prices have declined -48%, to $0.65 per million tokens, the lowest since at least January 2026.
Lower costs could unlock the next wave of AI adoption.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The total value of the US stock market has surged to 350% of the US M2 money supply, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The total value of the US stock market has surged to 350% of the US M2 money supply, the highest level since the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.
Since the 2022 bear market, this ratio has surged +170 percentage points.
Over this period, the S&P 500 has rallied +118%, while M2 has risen +9%.
In other words, the stock market's gain has outpaced the money supply growth by 13x.
The last time equity market growth exceeded M2 growth by a larger amount was from 1995 to 1999.
Asset owners are winning.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are betting on more upside in US Treasuries. The extra cost investors are willing to pay...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are betting on more upside in US Treasuries.
The extra cost investors are willing to pay for call options on longer-dated Treasuries relative to puts is up to ~50 basis points, the highest since March 2025.
This marks a sharp reversal from a 250-basis-point premium for puts over calls in late September.
This suggests investors are increasingly betting on further gains in Treasury prices.
Furthermore, one options trade is targeting a drop in the 10Y Note Yield to ~4.60% within a month, involving ~65,000 contracts and costing ~$7 million in premium.
This comes as the 10Y Note Yield has declined below 5.00% for the first time since September 23rd, now down -40 basis points from the October 7th peak.
The bond market is seeing massive swings in price and sentiment.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Do Podcasts Predict Elections? A Data-Driven Study 🔊 On the latest episode of The Prediction Marke...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Do Podcasts Predict Elections? A Data-Driven Study
🔊
On the latest episode of The Prediction Market Desk, Macro analyst Ryan Ricci @HedgeyeAI walked through a study testing whether podcast sentiment predicts where prediction markets move.
The premise is that people vote with their ears long before they get to the booth, so Ricci collected 976 episodes from the top podcasters with full YouTube shows over the past year, transcribed them, and ran them through an algorithm to score sentiment back to December.
The finding is that those sentiment scores lead Kalshi and the betting markets, with Trump criticism rising sharply in early January around the Iran war and leading the odds of Democrats taking the Senate at a 0.74 correlation.
Betrayal sentiment, podcasters who were active in electing Trump now saying they felt betrayed, spiked in that same January window and again in September.
One tell for the midterms, Ricci noted, is that the races barely came up in recent weeks, which may point to independents being unmotivated heading into the vote.
To watch the full episode, click here: https://app.hedgeye.com/events/188537-the-prediction-market-desk-politics-priced-in-real-time-episode-5?access%5B%5D=free

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang says “software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our compan...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA CEO Jensen Huang says “software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business.”
He said it could cost “about $2,000 per GPU per year” to run NVIDIA’s software for AI agents in these AI factories.
So, some napkin math at that price, before discounts:
500K licensed GPUs = $1B in annual revenue. 1 million licensed GPUs = $2B 5 million licensed GPUs = $10B
So, hypothetically, NVIDIA could earn billions a year from GPUs it has already sold by selling enterprise software and support to the companies using them.
Note: These are illustrative revenue scenarios using Jensen’s pricing example, not NVIDIA guidance or profit estimates.
item.content:encoded:
$NVDA CEO Jensen Huang says “software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business.”

He said it could cost “about $2,000 per GPU per year” to run NVIDIA’s software for AI agents in these AI factories.

So, some napkin math at that price, before discounts:

500K licensed GPUs = $1B in annual revenue.
1 million licensed GPUs = $2B
5 million licensed GPUs = $10B

So, hypothetically, NVIDIA could earn billions a year from GPUs it has already sold by selling enterprise software and support to the companies using them.

Note: These are illustrative revenue scenarios using Jensen’s pricing example, not NVIDIA guidance or profit estimates.

Global investor appetite for equities has never been stronger.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US government cannot afford higher interest rates. If interest rates average +150 basis points...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US government cannot afford higher interest rates.
If interest rates average +150 basis points above CBO’s February projections by 2036, US deficits would increase by nearly $6 trillion over this period.
The deficit would then rise to 8.8% of GDP, the highest level since WWII, excluding 2008 and 2020.
This would also push the US public Debt-to-GDP ratio to a record 133%, up from ~100% currently.
If rates average +50 basis points above projections, deficits would increase by nearly $2 trillion, lifting the Debt-to-GDP ratio to 124% by 2036.
Just weeks ago, the 10Y Note yield traded at ~5.30%, or ~100 basis points above CBO’s average projected rate over the next 10 years.
The US government needs rate cuts.

item.title: @wallstengine: CANVA JUST LAUNCHED ITS OWN AI IMAGE MODEL! It’s called Craft. Canva says it now ranks 2ND among im...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CANVA JUST LAUNCHED ITS OWN AI IMAGE MODEL!
It’s called Craft. Canva says it now ranks 2ND among image-generation labs on DesignArena, behind OpenAI.
It uses a two-stage process: a planner maps out the layout, objects and exact text from your prompt, then a separate renderer generates the image.
This approach is designed for work like posters, ads and product mockups, where readable text and precise placement matter. Canva refined the model using feedback from professional designers.
Craft supports up to 2K resolution and text in 55 languages. It is available now in Dream Lab, with public API access for developers.
item.content:encoded:
CANVA JUST LAUNCHED ITS OWN AI IMAGE MODEL!

It’s called Craft. Canva says it now ranks 2ND among image-generation labs on DesignArena, behind OpenAI.

It uses a two-stage process: a planner maps out the layout, objects and exact text from your prompt, then a separate renderer generates the image.

This approach is designed for work like posters, ads and product mockups, where readable text and precise placement matter. Canva refined the model using feedback from professional designers.

Craft supports up to 2K resolution and text in 55 languages. It is available now in Dream Lab, with public API access for developers.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: China purchased +25 tonnes of gold in August via the London OTC market, according to Gold...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China purchased +25 tonnes of gold in August via the London OTC market, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.
This is +25% more than the official +20 tonnes reported by China's central bank for this month.
This also follows estimated purchases of +35, +40, and +48 tonnes in July, June, and May, respectively.
Over these 4 months, China's estimated gold purchases through the OTC market exceeded officially reported purchases by 83 tonnes, or +128%.

China is stockpiling gold.

Over these 4 months, China's estimated gold purchases through the OTC market exceeded officially reported purchases by 83 tonnes, or +128%.

Meanwhile, global central banks are estimated to have acquired +79 tonnes of gold in August, +365% above the pre-2022 average of +17 tonnes.

China is stockpiling gold.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US energy stocks are having a historic year:
The S&P 500 Equal Weight Energy ETF, $RSPG, is up +49.2% YTD, trading near its all-time high.
$RSPG covers US energy sector stocks in the S&P 500, with each company receiving an approximately equal weight.
The fund is now on track for its 3rd-strongest annual return since its inception in 2006.
This would also mark its 6th consecutive annual gain, its longest winning streak on record.
Only two years have had higher returns, in 2021 and 2022, at +53.7% and +52.2%, respectively.
Over the last 2 weeks, $RSPG has risen +7.5%, and if that pace continues, the fund could record its strongest annual return since inception.
Energy stocks are thriving amid the Iran War.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -300,000 barrels last week, to 282.7 million b...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -300,000 barrels last week, to 282.7 million barrels, the lowest level since October 1982.
Since March 20th, US oil inventories in the SPR have dropped -132.8 million, or -32%.
We have now seen drawdowns in 29 of the last 30 weeks.
For perspective, oil reserves in the SPR stood at 653.9 million barrels in 2020, or +131% above current levels.
Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR dropped -3.1 million barrels last week, to 412.5 million barrels, the lowest reading since the end of July.
This is also ~3% below the 5-year average for this time of year.
America's oil stockpiles are at critically low levels.

item.description:
$NBIS SECURES $3.5 BILLION FINANCING FACILITY FROM CITI
Nebius announced a new senior secured credit facility to fund its global AI data center expansion and GPU purchases.
The facility has a 364-day maturity, with interest starting at SOFR + 2.75% and potentially rising to SOFR + 3.50%.
Nebius has more than $40 billion in long-term contracts with investment-grade customers, which could support additional asset-backed financing as it expands AI capacity in 2027 and beyond.

item.description:
DEEPSEEK RAISES $15 BILLION IN ONE OF CHINA’S LARGEST FUNDING ROUNDS
Chinese AI startup DeepSeek raised approximately 100 billion yuan, with Tencent and battery giant CATL among its biggest investors, according to Bloomberg.
The company initially targeted 50 billion yuan but doubled its fundraising goal amid strong investor demand.
DeepSeek is preparing for an IPO while increasing spending on AI data centers and open-source models to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The NAHB Housing Market Index fell -3 points in October, to 29, its lowest level since Ju...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The NAHB Housing Market Index fell -3 points in October, to 29, its lowest level since June 2012.
This marks the 2nd consecutive monthly decline in homebuilder sentiment, totaling -6 points, marking the largest 2-month decrease since June 2025.
All 3 components deteriorated, with current sales falling -2 points, to 33, the lowest since June 2012.
Sales expectations dropped -5 points, to 32, the lowest since November 2022, while buyer traffic plunged -5 points, to 18, the lowest since April 2012, excluding the 2020 pandemic.
Furthermore, 43% of builders cut prices this month, the highest proportion of any month from 2020 to 2026.
The affordability crisis is putting further pressure on homebuilder sentiment.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: The NAHB Housing Market Index fell -3 points in October, to 29, its lowest level since June 2012.

This marks the 2nd consecutive monthly decline in homebuilder sentiment, totaling -6 points, marking the largest 2-month decrease since June 2025.

All 3 components deteriorated, with current sales falling -2 points, to 33, the lowest since June 2012.

Sales expectations dropped -5 points, to 32, the lowest since November 2022, while buyer traffic plunged -5 points, to 18, the lowest since April 2012, excluding the 2020 pandemic.

Furthermore, 43% of builders cut prices this month, the highest proportion of any month from 2020 to 2026.

The affordability crisis is putting further pressure on homebuilder sentiment.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US private equity firms are struggling to attract new capital: Private equity funds raised just $22...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US private equity firms are struggling to attract new capital:
Private equity funds raised just $222 billion from investors in the first 9 months of 2026, on track for the weakest year since 2020.
This would also mark the 3rd consecutive annual decline.
By comparison, the industry attracted $406 billion in full year 2023 and $330 billion last year.
Higher rates have made it harder for private equity firms to sell businesses at attractive prices, weakening investment returns and prompting investors to become more reluctant to commit capital to new funds.
Smaller firms managing less than $15 billion are facing the most pressure.
Private equity has lost its shine in the rapidly evolving macroeconomic backdrop.

Smaller firms managing less than $15 billion are facing the most pressure.

Private equity has lost its shine in the rapidly evolving macroeconomic backdrop.

item.title: @wallstengine: PALANTIR & NVIDIA EXPAND SOVEREIGN AI DEPLOYMENTS Palantir $PLTR announced new AI deployments acros...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
PALANTIR & NVIDIA EXPAND SOVEREIGN AI DEPLOYMENTS
Palantir $PLTR announced new AI deployments across defense, construction, and healthcare, combining its AIP platform with $NVDA Nemotron models to help companies build AI using their own data.
Here's what companies are reporting:
> L3Harris unified over 30 ERP systems and says its AI models outperformed frontier models in internal testing while cutting costs by 95%.
> McCarthy Building trained AI on more than 100,000 construction RFIs and estimates its AI-assisted contract drafting could save 30,000 hours annually.
> Tampa General Hospital reported a 7% improvement in AI model performance and a 22x reduction in latency while keeping sensitive data local.
> Ondas launched Regna AI to help governments and enterprises develop mission-specific AI while retaining control of their data and infrastructure.
NVIDIA is also using Palantir AIP and customized Nemotron models to identify supply chain bottlenecks earlier and accelerate the process from wafer production to AI deployment.
item.content:encoded:
PALANTIR & NVIDIA EXPAND SOVEREIGN AI DEPLOYMENTS

Palantir $PLTR announced new AI deployments across defense, construction, and healthcare, combining its AIP platform with $NVDA Nemotron models to help companies build AI using their own data.

Here's what companies are reporting:

> L3Harris unified over 30 ERP systems and says its AI models outperformed frontier models in internal testing while cutting costs by 95%.

> McCarthy Building trained AI on more than 100,000 construction RFIs and estimates its AI-assisted contract drafting could save 30,000 hours annually.

> Tampa General Hospital reported a 7% improvement in AI model performance and a 22x reduction in latency while keeping sensitive data local.

> Ondas launched Regna AI to help governments and enterprises develop mission-specific AI while retaining control of their data and infrastructure.

NVIDIA is also using Palantir AIP and customized Nemotron models to identify supply chain bottlenecks earlier and accelerate the process from wafer production to AI deployment.

item.title: @wallstengine: TESLA CONFIRMS OPTIMUS HUMANOID ROBOT PRODUCTION HAS BEGUN $TSLA says its first production-quality...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TESLA CONFIRMS OPTIMUS HUMANOID ROBOT PRODUCTION HAS BEGUN
$TSLA says its first production-quality Optimus robots are now coming off high-volume manufacturing lines at its Fremont, California factory.
Tesla says its manufacturing process is now suitable for a commercial product, although hardware improvements will continue.
Production remains in the early ramp stage, while its Texas facility is still under construction.
Tesla has not disclosed production volumes or a timeline for full-scale manufacturing.
item.content:encoded:
TESLA CONFIRMS OPTIMUS HUMANOID ROBOT PRODUCTION HAS BEGUN

$TSLA says its first production-quality Optimus robots are now coming off high-volume manufacturing lines at its Fremont, California factory.

Tesla says its manufacturing process is now suitable for a commercial product, although hardware improvements will continue.

Production remains in the early ramp stage, while its Texas facility is still under construction.

Tesla has not disclosed production volumes or a timeline for full-scale manufacturing.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META CONFIRMS NEW NONVOTING SHARES TO FUND AI EXPANSION Meta announced it is creating a new Class...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META CONFIRMS NEW NONVOTING SHARES TO FUND AI EXPANSION
Meta announced it is creating a new Class C stock with no voting rights, allowing the company to raise money for AI investments, acquisitions, and employee compensation without reducing Mark Zuckerberg's voting control.
Existing shareholders will receive one new Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they own.
Meta says the distribution will have an effect similar to a 2-for-1 stock split on its current Class A share price, while leaving voting power unchanged.
The new stock class takes effect January 19, 2027, with plans to list the shares on Nasdaq.
The move comes as Meta expects capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, driven largely by its AI infrastructure expansion.
item.content:encoded:
$META CONFIRMS NEW NONVOTING SHARES TO FUND AI EXPANSION

Meta announced it is creating a new Class C stock with no voting rights, allowing the company to raise money for AI investments, acquisitions, and employee compensation without reducing Mark Zuckerberg's voting control.

Existing shareholders will receive one new Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they own.

Meta says the distribution will have an effect similar to a 2-for-1 stock split on its current Class A share price, while leaving voting power unchanged.

The new stock class takes effect January 19, 2027, with plans to list the shares on Nasdaq.

The move comes as Meta expects capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, driven largely by its AI infrastructure expansion.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries jumped +$83 billion in August, to $9.33 trillion, their...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries jumped +$83 billion in August, to $9.33 trillion, their 6th-highest total on record.
The surge was driven by Canada, which raised its holdings by +$38 billion, to $465 billion, its 4th-highest on record.
This was followed by Belgium, which increased its holdings by +$20 billion, to a record $491 billion.
The UK, the 2nd-largest holder, raised its holdings by +$11 billion, to a record $1.01 trillion.
Meanwhile, Japan, the largest foreign holder, cut its holdings by -$36 billion, to $1.07 trillion, its lowest since November 2024.
China, the 3rd-largest holder, reduced its holdings by -$27 billion, to $591 billion, its lowest level since August 2008.
Foreign holdings of US Treasuries are rising despite continued selling in Japan and China.
item.content:encoded:

This was followed by Belgium, which increased its holdings by +$20 billion, to a record $491 billion.

The UK, the 2nd-largest holder, raised its holdings by +$11 billion, to a record $1.01 trillion.

Meanwhile, Japan, the largest foreign holder, cut its holdings by -$36 billion, to $1.07 trillion, its lowest since November 2024.

China, the 3rd-largest holder, reduced its holdings by -$27 billion, to $591 billion, its lowest level since August 2008.

Foreign holdings of US Treasuries are rising despite continued selling in Japan and China.

item.title: @Hedgeye: The Poker Table Theory Of Short Covering 🔊 On the latest HAM for Lunch, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullou...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
The Poker Table Theory Of Short Covering
🔊
On the latest HAM for Lunch, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough and @HedgeyeAM Portfolio Managers Sam Rahman ($HGRO) @Hedgeye_HGRO and R. Patrick Kent ($HELS, $HEFT) @RPKInvestor broke down the anatomy of last week’s liquidation and what short covering really looks like.
The trigger was a $28 billion tech hedge fund liquidating over two to three days.
The setup heading into last week had been a barbell, leadership software and mega-cap tech on one side, semis as the hedge on the other. When the fund blew up, it didn’t just dump semis, it dumped its software winners too.
As Sam put it, Friday was “the poster child of what a liquidation looks like,” with every software name, mid and large, down five to 10%.
What rallies last in a breakdown is high short interest, and Keith’s framing is a poker table.
You’re playing against someone who’s “absolutely hammered and sucks at poker.”
It only gets worse as they have another drink, betting the wrong way, until they “finally just give up and go to bed,” or run out of money, or both.
That’s short covering, the moment the shorts stop working and the market frustrates you on the upside before rolling back over.
To watch the full episode, click here: https://app.hedgeye.com/insights/188508-ham-for-lunch-where-we-see-opportunity-and-risk-in-today-s-markets?type=%2C

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the 2nd-lowest reading since May 2020.
This follows MoM declines of -4.9% and -5.9% in July and August.
Single-family housing starts dropped -4.6% MoM last month, to 859,000, the 2nd-lowest since April 2023.
At the same time, multifamily housing starts fell -7.2%, to 349,000, the 2nd-lowest since May 2025.
Higher mortgage rates and worsening affordability are heavily weighing on housing demand.
Furthermore, elevated housing inventories and falling homebuilder confidence are discouraging new construction.
The US housing market is frozen.

item.title: @cultured: Whop has raised $200M in Series D funding at a $5.1B valuation, backed by @sequoia and @shopify. It...
item.dc:creator: @cultured
item.description:
Whop has raised $200M in Series D funding at a $5.1B valuation, backed by @sequoia and @shopify.
It really feels like we are barely touching the tip of the iceberg in a market larger than anyone can imagine.
We first launched Whop as a better way for us to sell sneaker bots, one of the most niche types of desktop software out there.
Total TAM? Probably $20,000 per day.
Who cares, tiny market.
But, what people discounted is the idea that there were actually 70,000 other markets exactly like that one.
Beyond the investment itself, I am especially excited to welcome legendary silicon valley investor @dougleone to our board of directors. Doug and the sequoia team are nothing but a brilliant, resourceful, and principled group of people.
My co-founder Cameron and I started building on Shopify when we were 13 years old. Shopify is one of the most impactful all-in-one cloud ecosystems ever created; @tobi has pioneered modern entrepreneurship the way we know it and we are thrilled to have him in our corner.
We have a tenet at Whop to be the dumbest in the room and I am very grateful that this has recently become a lot easier.
We are focused on markets, scale economies, and progressive media. If that is up your alley, please message me directly.
The $200M raised will support our expansion as we build economic infrastructure for the next century, continuing on our mission of delivering everyone an income.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing. US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is u...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing.
US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is up to $419 billion so far in 2026, the highest annual figure on record.
This represents a +90% YoY increase from full-year 2025 and a +437% increase from full-year 2024.
Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Oracle, $ORCL, have issued a combined $157 billion in corporate bonds, accounting for 37% of the total.
This is followed by investment-grade and high-yield data center and computing companies, which have raised $66 billion and $37 billion, respectively, and together account for ~25% of AI-related issuance.
Other AI-linked corporate bonds have represented $159 billion, or 38%.
The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

Falconer is launching an AI knowledge base that helps keep company information up to date for employees and AI agents.
It connects GitHub, Slack, documents and meetings. When code changes, Falconer identifies affected documentation and drafts updates for review. Teams can also enable automatic updates for eligible documents.
Employees and agents can ask questions in Falconer or Slack and get answers with source citations. Its Knowledge Health dashboard flags outdated information, gaps and contradictions.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Tokenization is accelerating. There are now over 360 onchain tokenized equity products, up +200% YT...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tokenization is accelerating.
There are now over 360 onchain tokenized equity products, up +200% YTD.
10 of these products have exceeded $100 million in tokenized supply.
As we saw this weekend, demand for 24/7 access to equities is rapidly expanding.
In fact, the majority of volume in these tokenized products, at ~60%, is currently taking place outside of regular market hours.
Today, onchain giant Jupiter, a leader in this space, reported a +215% quarter-over-quarter jump in tokenized equity trade count.
We expect more record highs ahead in this space.

item.title: @wallstengine: NVIDIA & VERTIV TARGET UP TO 30% MORE AI TOKENS WITH THE SAME CAPACITY $NVDA and $VRT announced a n...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA & VERTIV TARGET UP TO 30% MORE AI TOKENS WITH THE SAME CAPACITY
$NVDA and $VRT announced a new AI factory deployment approach at GTC Berlin that could cut the time from project kickoff to productive capacity from 120 days to just 48 days.
According to Vertiv's modeled estimates, this could result in up to 30% more cumulative AI token output in the first 12 months, without increasing installed computing capacity.
Here's how the new approach works:
• 10x Faster Design: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory reference design, Omniverse DSX Blueprint, and Vertiv's SimReady assets integrate with Dassault Systèmes' 3DEXPERIENCE platform to reduce configuration and validation time from 30 days to just 3 days.
• 50% Faster Deployment: Vertiv's prefabricated OneCore and SmartRun infrastructure could reduce on-site power and cooling deployment from 90 days to 45 days.
• 72 Days Saved: Combined, the approach could bring AI factories online approximately 10 weeks earlier, providing 317 productive days in the first year compared with 245 using conventional methods.
• Real-World Deployment: Polar Data Centers is applying Vertiv's factory-built approach to the first 41 MW phase of its AI data center in Herøya, Norway 🇳🇴, with plans to scale the facility to 100 MW.
• Factory-Built Infrastructure: Power, cooling, networking, and supporting systems can be designed and virtually validated before construction, with more assembly and testing completed off-site.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: This is unprecedented. Micron, $MU, and Nvidia, $NVDA are expected to account for 36% of the S&P 50...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
This is unprecedented.
Micron, $MU, and Nvidia, $NVDA are expected to account for 36% of the S&P 500’s earnings growth in Q3 2026 earnings season.
This comes as $MU and $NVDA are expected to contribute +5.2 and +4.6 percentage points to the index’s +27% YoY earnings growth, respectively.
Meanwhile, the next 8 top contributors are projected to add +8.2 percentage points, accounting for ~30% of the estimated S&P 500’s net income growth.
Then, the remaining 490 stocks are set to contribute just +9.2 percentage points, representing 34% of the index’s projected earnings growth.
Excluding those top 10 contributors, earnings growth is estimated to decline -11% YoY in Q3.
Never in history have we witnessed market concentration like this.

item.title: @wallstengine: AGILE ROBOTS UNVEILS NVIDIA-POWERED HUMANOID, TARGETS UP TO 2,000 ROBOTS IN 2027 Germany's 🇩🇪 Agi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AGILE ROBOTS UNVEILS NVIDIA-POWERED HUMANOID, TARGETS UP TO 2,000 ROBOTS IN 2027
Germany's 🇩🇪 Agile Robots unveiled Agile ONE SN at $NVDA's GTC Berlin, a new humanoid robot built for AI research and development.
CEO Zhaopeng Chen told Reuters the company plans to produce between 1,000 and 2,000 humanoid robots across its ONE S and ONE SN models in 2027, with production expected to begin by the end of 2026.
Here are the key features:
• Size: Stands 1.4 meters (4.6 feet) tall and weighs 40 kg (88 lbs), according to NVIDIA, with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3 kg payload per arm.
• Hands: Two five-fingered WUJI Hand 2 robotic hands, each with 20 degrees of freedom, tactile sensing, and 1kHz force control for precise manipulation.
• AI Computing: Powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control.
• Vision and Sensors: Equipped with head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors, and inertial measurement units to perceive and interact with its environment.
• AI Software: Comes preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, providing AI models and tools for robot learning, training, and whole-body control.
• Safety: Planned integration with NVIDIA Halos to support safer robot operation and deployment.
• Development: NVIDIA says the preconfigured platform can reduce setup time for researchers from weeks to days.
• Availability: Expected in early 2027, with Stanford University and ETH Zurich among institutions showing interest.
“The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale,” CEO Zhaopeng Chen said.

item.title: @wallstengine: GOOGLE CLOUD & NVIDIA PLAN TO SCALE VERA RUBIN INFRASTRUCTURE TO UP TO 960,000 GPUS Google Cloud an...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GOOGLE CLOUD & NVIDIA PLAN TO SCALE VERA RUBIN INFRASTRUCTURE TO UP TO 960,000 GPUS
Google Cloud announced that its new A5X instances, powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, will become generally available next month, with plans to expand availability to Europe.
The new infrastructure is designed to support large-scale AI training, inference, autonomous AI agents, and reinforcement learning.
Here's what was announced:
• 960,000 Rubin GPUs: Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin infrastructure to as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple data center sites.
• A5X Instances: Combine NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud's Virgo networking, and fourth-generation liquid cooling to support demanding AI workloads.
• Ineffable Intelligence: The company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver became the first customer to access A5X, using it to develop "superlearners" that continuously improve through experience.
• WPP: Tested AI-powered creative workflows using NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenShell on A5X. Initial tests showed that workloads previously requiring a multi-node cluster could run on a single A5X instance.
• Confidential Computing: Google Cloud is also expanding secure AI infrastructure, making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with plans to bring rack-scale capabilities to GB300 NVL72-powered A4X Max instances.
Google Cloud and NVIDIA are also exploring new power-efficiency technologies through NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS to support larger AI deployments within existing data center power limits.

• Confidential Computing: Google Cloud is also expanding secure AI infrastructure, making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with plans to bring rack-scale capabilities to GB300 NVL72-powered A4X Max instances.

Google Cloud and NVIDIA are also exploring new power-efficiency technologies through NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS to support larger AI deployments within existing data center power limits.

item.title: @wallstengine: NVIDIA & AMKOR $AMKR PLAN OVER 300% EXPANSION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING CAPACITY NVIDIA announced new a...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA & AMKOR $AMKR PLAN OVER 300% EXPANSION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING CAPACITY
NVIDIA announced new agreements with major semiconductor supply chain partners at GTC Berlin to expand manufacturing capacity for its current and next-generation AI platforms.
Here's what's planned:
• Amkor: Increase advanced packaging interposer wafer capacity in South Korea by more than 300% by the end of 2028, alongside new manufacturing facilities.
• IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Unimicron: Expand substrate capacity by 2.5x over the next three years, with production expansions across Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan.
• KYEC: Build new semiconductor testing facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. High-volume production is targeted for April 2027.
• SPIL: Increase optical-engine manufacturing capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with plans to double it again by the end of 2028.
• Semiconductor Testing: NVIDIA expects its overall testing capacity to double from 2026 to 2027, supported by expansions in the U.S., Taiwan, and Singapore.
Jensen Huang said:
“We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint.”
The expansion is intended to increase production capacity and strengthen NVIDIA's global supply chain as demand for AI infrastructure continues to grow.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA ANNOUNCES MAJOR EXPANSION OF ITS ISAAC ROBOTICS PLATFORM, INCLUDING A NEW HUMANOID ROBOT “the...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA ANNOUNCES MAJOR EXPANSION OF ITS ISAAC ROBOTICS PLATFORM, INCLUDING A NEW HUMANOID ROBOT
“the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching.”
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA introduced new humanoid robotics technology, AI training tools, simulation datasets, and software designed to accelerate the development of general-purpose robots.
Here's what's new:
• Agile ONE SN: A new humanoid reference robot developed by Agile Robots, powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Isaac GR00T. It stands 1.4 meters tall, weighs 40 kg, features 31 degrees of freedom, and has two five-finger hands. Expected in early 2027.
• Isaac Lab 3.0: Now generally available, enabling developers to train and refine robot behaviors using multi-GPU workflows and physics-based simulation.
• Isaac OS: A new open-source runtime connecting AI models, sensors, controls, and robot hardware for real-time operation.
• New Training Data: More than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, alongside the Human 1M Dataset containing human activity videos and 3D hand-tracking data.
• DGX Station: Three new open-source workflows for improving GR00T models through reinforcement learning, developing complex manipulation skills, and generating synthetic training data using NVIDIA Cosmos.
Companies including ABB Robotics, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Universal Robots, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, and Sereact are building on NVIDIA's technologies for industrial robotics applications.

item.title: @wallstengine: Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's DSX POD could cut the time from AI hardware arrival to producing tokens...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's DSX POD could cut the time from AI hardware arrival to producing tokens from four to five months down to about one month.
He says a one-gigawatt AI data center costs $50 billion and is expected to generate $40 billion in annual revenue, meaning a three-month delay could cost $10 billion in revenue.
“$10 billion worth of revenues will make anybody anxious.”
Jensen explained:
“And so by moving this into the supply chain, the speed by which we can turn on go from installation, arrival of computing to production of tokens will go from many months. We think something along the lines of 4 to 5 months down to about a month.”
“Okay, so this is a complete transformation of the world's supply chain and this will change the way that people install and build data centers.”
“And hopefully as a result, velocity goes up, the wasted idle compute, the wasted idle CapEx will reduce and everybody becomes more profitable.”

item.title: @wallstengine: Jensen Huang just showed how NVIDIA and Anthropic are working together to make AI agents more secur...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Jensen Huang just showed how NVIDIA and Anthropic are working together to make AI agents more secure with $NVDA OpenShell and Claude Managed Agents.
OpenShell allows AI agents to operate inside secure sandboxes while controlling exactly what they can access and do.
Here's how it works:
• Controls which files, tools, networks, and private data AI agents can access.
• Blocks actions by default unless explicitly permitted by security policies.
• Monitors agent activity and logs every allowed or blocked action.
• Allows companies to run agent execution inside their own infrastructure, keeping sensitive data and code within their environment.
• Uses a policy prover to mathematically verify what resources an agent can access.
With Claude Managed Agents, Anthropic handles agent orchestration while NVIDIA OpenShell adds security controls inside the execution environment.
NVIDIA OpenShell is open source, while Claude Managed Agents is available in public beta.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value.
By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the 15 largest stocks accounted for 27.2% of the S&P 500.
The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3% of the S&P 500’s market cap.
This comes as Nvidia, $NVDA, Apple, $AAPL, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, account for 7.5%, 7.1%, 5.9%, and 5.6%, respectively, or 26.1% combined.
This means just 4 stocks account for more than the next 11 combined.
Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.
Market concentration is at historic extremes.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global debt crisis has never been worse. Japan now has a gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio of...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global debt crisis has never been worse.
Japan now has a gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio of 204.4%, the highest among any major world economy.
Italy follows at 138.4%, while the United States stands at 125.8%, which is only below the ~132.0% record set during the 2020 pandemic.
At the same time, France’s gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio is 118.4%, while Canada’s, China’s, and the UK’s are 110.7%, 106.9%, and 103.6%, respectively.
By comparison, Germany is the only major economy below 100.0%, at 64.6%.
The current average among advanced economies is 108.2%.
The world economy is drowning in debt.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US affordability crisis is worsening: Food prices have surged +34.5% since December 2019, now a...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US affordability crisis is worsening:
Food prices have surged +34.5% since December 2019, now at their highest level on record.
Rent and grocery prices have risen +33.3% and +30.0%, respectively.
Furthermore, motor vehicle maintenance and repair prices have soared +55.2% over the same period.
Meanwhile, prices for services excluding rent, including medical care, transportation, education, communication, and recreation, have increased +29.2% since December 2019.
As a result, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) has risen +30.4%.
Basic necessities are becoming increasingly unaffordable in the US.

5-day sales were 2.6 standard deviations above the average over the last 12 months.
Over this period, the largest sales were recorded in the US technology sector, with semiconductor stocks accounting for 57% of US tech sales.
Meanwhile, in just 1 week, hedge funds reversed all cumulative purchases of AI stocks since the start of 2025, erasing nearly 2 years of accumulation in this group.
Despite the sales, hedge fund net exposure to global tech stocks remains higher than it has been 90% of the time over the last 5 years.
Hedge funds are reducing their exposure to tech at a record pace.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Why Hedge Funds Are Getting Blindsided By This Market
🔊
On The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough and Director of Research Daryl Jones @HedgeyeDJ covered why factors are wreaking havoc on hedge funds.
The spark was Citadel’s head of global equities, Justin Lobell, noting that even though the S&P hasn’t moved much, it’s the factor moves getting people offsides and blowing up books.
One of the first charts Hedgeye ever built 18 years ago was factors, and those moves have crushed people.
For Keith, it’s non-negotiable.
As he put it, “if you don’t have factors on your screens,” rather than something like the Dow and points, “you should not be gainfully employed.”
No NHL player uses a wooden stick and nobody takes a horse and buggy to work, yet in markets people still lean on moving averages and valuation models instead of factors, flows, and gamma.
The managers who wouldn’t evolve are effectively extinct, and however this AI bubble ends, loaded with levered ETFs and short-dated options, factors will be the defining feature of it.

item.title: @wallstengine: Beacon has launched an open-source memory system for AI coding agents, alongside a $5.5 million see...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Beacon has launched an open-source memory system for AI coding agents, alongside a $5.5 million seed round announced by its team.
The software captures coding sessions and converts useful debugging patterns, fixes and corrections into reusable skills. It supports more than 20 coding tools, including Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
Beacon uses decision models such as Jev to identify information worth retaining. Developers can also start a task in Claude Code and continue it in Codex with one command, transferring context between tools. https://x.com/jqdsouza/status/2112552451547001218/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US electricity prices are skyrocketing. The average price of US residential electricity has risen +...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US electricity prices are skyrocketing.
The average price of US residential electricity has risen +11% since January 2025, to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, near an all-time high.
Average prices during the first 8 months of 2026 were +40% higher than in the same period of 2019.
The largest increase in residential electricity prices over this period was in Maine, at +90%, followed by California and New York, at nearly +70%.
This comes as the AI boom is intensifying electricity demand, with data centers requiring enormous amounts of electricity to power thousands of chips and cooling systems.
A 1-gigawatt data center can consume as much electricity as 800,000 homes.
As a result, wholesale electricity prices in areas near significant data center activity surged by as much as +267% between 2020 and 2025.
The AI revolution is driving a surge in electricity demand, and households are increasingly feeling the cost.
